utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning. Mr. Karadzic, please continue. Please plan your statement so as to leave about ten minutes at the end of today's hearing for a Chamber's oral ruling.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellencies. As we saw yesterday, in an incredible rhythm or a shocking rhythm that prevailed in Croatia, there was a shocking measure introduced each month affecting the Serbs. The same situation was with us. Before I come to the October declaration adopted by the SDA and HDZ deputies contrary to the way the Assembly sessions are convened and contrary to the provisions of the constitutions of Yugoslavia and Bosnia and Herzegovina, as a follow-up I would just like to add that the SDS was the last ethnic party to be established. We did that reluctantly, because we didn't think that ethnic democracy was a proper thing, but we were forced by the events to do so. The elections took place on the 18th of November, and each nationalist party won, because all the peoples adopted ethnic differentiations based partly on fears and partly on the hopes and ambitions that they would achieve something that they hadn't had before in Yugoslavia. The government was formed in January 1991, and the first campaign for an independent Bosnia-Herzegovina started in January, although Mr. Izetbegovic vowed to remain in Yugoslavia in January as well. In late January, he suddenly announced the campaign for independence. Then in February, Mr. Izetbegovic formed a secret council for the defence of Muslims, although he was the chairman of the public council for defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I will only state briefly that during the first campaign for independence the Serbs protested without resorting to countermeasures. Izetbegovic formed this Council, which acted as the Supreme Command of the Patriotic League, the secret army of the SDA. The Serbian reaction was astonishment, concern, without either protests or countermeasures, because it had been done secretly. We found out about it, but we did not protest much because of it. There was an attempt in February to adopt a declaration on sovereignty and independence. The Serbs protested and filed a veto and referred the matter to the Council for Ethnic Equality, and the veto succeeded at that time, it was adopted, and we announced that we were going to work on communities of municipalities because if the municipalities decided to do so, they could associate themselves if they had economic and other interests. The Patriotic League was established on the 31st of March, and the Supreme Command now has its army. The Serbs were deeply concerned over this. The Serbs employed in the police and the MUP that were brought into power, although they were not members of the SDS because we don't think that there were -- should be any political affiliations in the police. They tried to prevent any abuse of the police and to inform the public about what was going on. This was the first time that we in a way had some misunderstandings with our deputy minister that we nominated for that position. So in March 1991, a second attempt to adopt a declaration on independence took place. After these consultations with our partners, we lodged a veto and continued consultations with the municipalities. Famously, the declaration on the sovereignty of Bosnia-Herzegovina will be passed with or without the Serbian delegates is what Alija Izetbegovic said in May 1991. So in three months' time, we had used up all of our brotherhood and unity, our idyllic coalition, and the breaching of all our rights was announced. And the abuse of the police force gathered pace. Their police was full of criminals, and you heard yesterday from my conversation with the deputy minister in which he agreed that we didn't bring any new personnel to the police, unlike them, and we particularly didn't bring in any criminals as they did. The SDA personnel in the police were keeping everything secret from the Serbs. They assigned Serbs to unimportant positions, and kept them away from all the illegal activities that they were involved in, and that was the first split that happened in the MUP in May 1991. It was a de facto, not a de jure division of the MUP. The Serbian personnel in the police were sidetracked so that they could not have any influence, so that they had no insight into the events, let alone any influence on them. The Serbs reacted by forming autonomous Serbian regions. The Serbian autonomous areas were proclaimed, but this had no substance. They were not functioning as such; nothing was going on. They were there just in case if something happened. And if communications are cut off, the people would be severed from their leadership, and they, in that case, should have some regional leadership to lead them. In June 1991, decisions were taken on this independence of Slovenia and Croatia, and Kucan, Tudjman and Izetbegovic concluding a secret agreement to attack the JNA and Yugoslavia. This conspiracy and this secret pact will be confirmed here thanks to the evidence provided by the Prosecution, and we also have our own sources of information. The Serbian reaction was to accelerate the creation of SAOs and there's already talk about regionalisation and we thought that they should start functioning because this was no joke any longer. All our moves were conditional even though the SDA’s were not. These were not our goals. That was done out of necessity. If you continue this way and do not nullify these unlawful decisions, we are going to activate our plans. The German newspapers "Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung" and "Die Welt" wrote about Yugoslavia, that it was a historical freak, created through agreements from the Paris conference, and they --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Periphery, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and they were mocking the Versailles, Saint- Germain, Trianon, and the Neuilly agreements that ended the First World War. Let me remind you that in 1977 and 1978, while Tito was still alive, Josef Strauss gathered the European elite in Munich and tried to persuade them to proclaim Yugoslavia dead. By courtesy of General Gallois we acquired this information. General Gallois is an exceptional personality who didn't agree with that either then or now. In July, the Serbs published a document, in Serbian and in English, entitled What Do the Serbs Propose? Now, I wonder why the Prosecution doesn't mention this agreement at all and why they didn't want to learn what the Serbian position was vis-a-vis Yugoslavia and Bosnia-Herzegovina. What do the Serbs propose? It was an important moment. The crisis was accelerating and the Serbs proposed a solution for the Bosnian crisis. This proposal excludes absolutely any possibility or any notion of a joint criminal venture -- enterprise. It absolutely precludes the possibility of an outcome such as the one that stands in the Indictment. In the beginning of July, the Muslim-Bosniak organisation led by Adil Zulfikarpasic and Muhamed Filipovic who had left the SDA once they learnt about the conspiracy that was being pursued behind the backs of the whole party and the whole Muslim people. When Filipovic and Zulfikarpasic, as experienced politicians and dissidents of long standing, needed some time to see where all these moves were leading to, this led Mr. Causevic, after leaving the SDA, to say to Mr. Izetbegovic the following: "Do you think that the Serbs are fools who cannot see what you're doing?" The Serb side was delighted with this proposal of a historic Serbian-Muslim agreement, and they decided to abandon all the counter-measures that they had envisaged. Early July, proof that we abandoned these counter-measures, conceived in order to thwart the violation of our constitutional rights, once that the Muslim side offered to abandon the path it had taken. Mr. Zulfikarpasic and I met with Mr. Izetbegovic, who said, Just go on. And he said to Zulfikarpasic, Please continue your work because the Serbs don't trust me any longer and maybe you can achieve something. In July and August of 1991, we were working on this historic Serbian-Muslim agreement. We had joint meetings that were full of tensions, but the leaderships of the SDS and the MBO were visiting sensitive areas such as Trebinje and they're holding rallies there. But everybody was happy, both the Serbs and the Muslims. Then we went to Zvornik, which was also a sensitive area, which exploded at a later stage. Apart from a small number of extremists, people were delighted. We had a crowded sports hall, and they were happy to see that there was a change in the relations between the Serbs and the Muslims. The Serbs accepted the return of the status quo ante, and during this six-month period we didn't apply any counter-measures that we had envisaged because we reached an agreement with the Muslims. Towards the end of August, all of a sudden Mr. Izetbegovic withdrew his support to this agreement while Professor Koljevic and Professor Filipovic, both from the philosophical faculty, who were authorised by Zulfikarpasic and myself to continue our work, presented this agreement to the public with a view to relaxing the situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina, to say that Bosnia is a tripartite state, Bosnian Croats and Muslims, and to convince them that there were no problems, although there were conflicts in Croatia already going on, but they said that this would prevent spill-over into Bosnia. A fax arrived during the middle of a broadcast that the SDA was withdrawing, and the MBO and Mr. Filipovic were proclaimed traitors of the Muslim nation. So all this game of trying to deceive the Muslims and the Serbs with the aim of defeating politically the MBO, that would have amounted to a Pyrrhus victory. That was a costly and dearly victory. Immediately the following day, tensions rose in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the Serbian side, particularly the autonomous region of Krajina, without asking us anything about it, proclaimed an Autonomous Region of the Krajina. We have an intercept on this subject, and we can always show it to the Trial Chamber should they find it of interest. After that, Izetbegovic withdrew, and we adopted a declaration in the Assembly whose basic elements were, firstly, that all options should be treated as equal; and secondly, that there would be no imposition of solutions by any party. A solution had to be found that would be acceptable for everyone involved without any imposition and all options were legitimate. So this relaxed the situation a bit, but it didn't last longer than a month. By mid-October we have this famous Assembly session where a constitutional coup d'etat took place where the continuation of the session was convened unlawfully and all the Serbian deputies, 83 of them, 72 from the SDS and the Serbs from other multi-ethnic parties, walked out of the Assembly, and the Serbian side announced that unless these decisions were revoked within a week, then the Serbian side was going to establish their own Assembly as a kind of personal autonomy. This is a pivotal moment for both the Prosecution and the indictment. In paragraph 34 of the pre-trial brief, the Prosecution says the leadership of the Bosnian Serbs established on the 24th of October, 1991, a separate Serbian Assembly. As Karadzic explained to the delegates, this was an historic move which dispelled the last illusions that the Serbs might have. It will help them to recognise who their friends or foes were, and they will never again be threatened from internal forces. So Karadzic said this is the point when we gave up on all our illusions. We know exactly who our enemies and who our friends are, and we know exactly where threats are coming from. Therefore, in November 1991, again in paragraph 34, it reads that immediately before the SDS plebiscite on which the Serbs confirmed that they wanted to remain in Yugoslavia, Karadzic invited the municipal authorities to establish their own power in their respective areas. "Please be very energetic in pursuing this policy and establish power in your territories; in municipalities, regions and local communes, and prepare yourselves for restructuring and reorganising the municipalities." This is a quotation of my words by the Prosecution. But this does not have the meaning that was attributed to by the OTP. I'd like to remind you that between the 24th of October, when the Serbs realised where the SDS was leading the nation, the Serbs accepted before the beginning of the war several chances and options for peace, and they even were prepared to give up on their own Assembly. So Serbs established an Assembly as their last defence. If all else failed, they would have that Assembly. As the Trial Chamber says in the Krajisnik judgement, paragraph 195 or 196, if the old system fell apart, the central government has to do something in order to prevent the ground from falling apart. And what is stated here is: "Prepare and establish authority in your own territories, in the municipalities." If the central government fails and if the municipalities have no one to rely upon; or if they call the central government, and the central government issues them orders that are contrary to the survival of the people, then we have to establish the authorities. We already have our authorities there but they have to be prepared to function in extraordinary circumstances. I believe, and I think that all international documents corroborate that, that it is better to have any kind of authority than no authority at all. Chaos is the worst that you can have. It is no longer only the SDS that represents the Serbs. All the Serbs are there, and they schedule a plebiscite for November 1991. Let us see whether the people want what Izetbegovic is insisting upon, or do the people want something else. The referendum question has to do with Yugoslavia, with the joining of all who wish to remain in Yugoslavia, and that referendum was indeed held. Since this was an ethnic referendum, there was a possibility for others to vote as well, and indeed, between 40 to 60.000 Muslims and Croats did vote, and -- in the referendum, and they voted in favour of preserving Yugoslavia. I am afraid that the Prosecution is being malicious when they say that this was a yellow leaflet. I don't know what the colour of this ballot or leaflet was, but it was written in the Latin script. Most Serbs use the Cyrillic script, but it was printed in Latin so that they would find it more pleasant, as it were. Now, on the 20th of December, the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina, contrary to the position and opinion of all Serb ministers and deputy ministers who were members of the government, passed a decision to ask the European Community to recognise an independent Bosnia-Herzegovina. There are no prerequisites for that. That decision was not made in the right way. It could not have been reached at the referendum either, because two -- less than two-thirds of all voters voted in favour of that, and it also couldn't pass through the Assembly because we had more than one third. And it's not a government that asks for independence. It can only be an Assembly on the basis of more than two-thirds of all MP votes. As for the Serbian reaction at the Assembly session of 21 November, we are going to make you aware of each and every detail of this Assembly, because it is often exploited in the Indictment. They asked for an annulment of this request for independence, or, as a counter measure, they're going to proclaim a Serb republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Let us have a look at this map. The Serbs are blue. This was 1991. It didn't change much. That's basically the way it was. After the genocide in the Second World War, the Serbs continued to live in two -- they are a majority, rather, in two-thirds of the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and regrettably they have only one-third. Up until the Second World War they were the majority population. The SDA refuses to withdraw this request and they move on. From the 20th of December until the 9th of January, they were given 20 days to decide. The Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina was proclaimed, but like all other Serb measures it is only proclaimed as a possibility. It doesn't really function. So the Prosecution is not right when they believe that we established the Assembly of the Serb people in order to achieve some objectives. We are actually right. We established the Serb Assembly in order to prevent the SDA from achieving their objectives at the expense of our security and our own will. We can see on the basis of all the interim steps taken, and one of the interim steps was the Assembly that was held on the 24th and 25th of January, where Karadzic and Cengic -- this is Muhamed Cengic from the SDA. It's not the MBO anymore. The MBO all the time was in favour of reaching an agreement with the Serbs. Now the vice-president of the SDA, Cengic, we mentioned that yesterday, reaches agreement with me at the rostrum itself. This is very well-known footage. We all agree at the same time that the government carries out a regionalisation within 15 days, and the Serbs vote in the referendum. Whatever they do, they vote and in this way give the referendum legitimacy. Izetbegovic initiated the agreement because Cengic publicly said that it was Izetbegovic who authorised him in this manner. It lasted only for two hours. With the MBO, the agreement lasted for two months; whereas this one lasted for only two hours. Now what happens? February, the conference starts. Although we had been receiving monitors from the EU a lot earlier, like Ambassador Wijnaendts, Ambassador Cutileiro, Lord Carrington, et cetera, but officially it is in February that the conference started, and on the 22nd or 23rd of February, definitely what is reached is an agreement on three Bosnias. The Serbs said, "Right. We are going to leave Yugoslavia. We are going to leave Yugoslavia and remain within the framework of these boundaries of Bosnia-Herzegovina once they are recognised on the condition that we get this one unit inside and that Bosnia is a compound decentralised state where Serbs, Croats, and Muslims are going to have those guarantees and that security that the republics in Yugoslavia had, however, at a far lower level." On the 22nd or 23rd of February, a decision was made to the effect that the future constituent units will have their own powers. Inter alia, they will have the right to their autonomous sovereign police that is accountable only to that government and that Assembly. Since we had experience already to the effect that, say, yesterday we reach agreement on ten points, and Mr. Izetbegovic the next day comes and says that we had agreed to nothing, zero. We say if we agreed on ten questions, tomorrow we discuss the eleventh question. We cannot go back to square one yet again. It was only in 1993 that we adopted the principle that nothing has been agreed upon until everything is agreed upon. Until then, whatever had been adopted could be put into force. Then the Assembly reaches a decision. The Serb Assembly and the council of ministers, on the 28th of February, decides that preparations are carried out for establishing a Serb MUP. And why immediately after the agreement? Because there was massive, massive abuse of the joint police. The Muslim police, they were wreaking havoc. We can see that as testified by Prosecution witnesses, that the police, the Muslim part of the police, and the SDA and the Patriotic League had all become one, and you cannot distinguish between different institutions anymore, but we will go back to this abuse. So on the 28th of February and on the 1st of March there was a referendum. The Serbs did not vote in the referendum, but they didn't prevent it from happening either. We had our own in November, our plebiscite. We believed it was all right to have this too, when they had already scheduled it, but we considered it a two- ethnic, bi-ethnic referendum, and not a referendum of the citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina, for that it was not. Because it did not happen in a lawful way. On the 1st of March, criminals, well-known criminals, notorious criminals, who are now activists of the Patriotic League, they killed the members of a wedding party in front of the old church, where they wrote graffiti against the Serbs on the very next day after the establishment of the SDA was announced. This old church was built during the days of the Turkish occupation. The anecdote says that the Sultan said, All right, you can build a church that will be as big as the skin of an ox. And then, allegedly, the Serbs cut this skin of an ox into a thread and in this way circled the area where the church would be built. The Sultan also said that it should not be higher than even the lowest minaret of all the mosques. They built the church partly underground, so you really have to walk downstairs when you walk into the church. I hope you go to Sarajevo one day. So watch your step when you go there. You go very deep down into the ground. This is church that is very dear to the hearts of the Serbs. Anyway, the Muslims tried to engage in deceit and say that this was not an active church. It was always an active church, even in the days of the Turks, and even the Turks did not touch it. So a young man hits Nikola Gardovic, the father of the bridegroom on that day, and already the next day he appears on TV as a hero, and he said, "Yes, I shot at him. Why would he carry a Serb flag?" Serb flags were carried even in the Turkish days at weddings. It was not a national flag. It was a religious flag and it was customary. Then on the 2nd of March, barricades were put up in Sarajevo. At the time, Mr. Koljevic, Mr. Krajisnik and I are negotiating in Belgrade. So we were not there. Barricades were put up, and they were there for two days. The SDS did negotiate with the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina with regard to these barricades, and the Crisis Staff that was headed by this gentleman, who was arrested in London just now, Mr. Ejup Ganic. He was a member of the Presidency, a Yugoslav who turned against Yugoslavia. So in this situation rife with tension, on 18th of March, an agreement was reached, the Lisbon Agreement. The Cutileiro Peace Plan was adopted, stating that this territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina would be reorganised with three internal units of the Serb, Croat, and Muslim people, and we all celebrate. May I remind you that Mr. Ajanovic celebrated the most, saying that 80 to 85 per cent of all Muslims will be in their constituent unit, and only about 20 per cent of the Serbs and Croats would be in their unit, whereas the Serbs fared the worst. Only 50-something per cent will be in the Serb unit, whereas the rest would be scattered throughout Bosnia. Even then or after that, no one referred to any population exchanges or any expulsions. On the 24th of March, the SDA withdrew their agreement. I remind you that on the 18th of March, Ajanovic said, If the Serbs refuse this agreement this is going to be yet another foolish thing that they are doing, and it will be proof that they had opted for war. However, a week later they are the ones that annul the Lisbon Agreement. Mr. Ajanovic says, Well, we did this sort of as a trick in order to buy time, to wait for recognition, to wait for international recognition at that. Perhaps we could have a look at this slide. Could we have the previous one, actually. Yes. "If the Serbian Assembly rejects the Cutileiro Plan, it will become evident who is against peace in Bosnia, and it will become evident who wants to trick the European Community and the chairman of the conference." Lord Carrington, that is. Excellencies, this is an admission: Who does that will be guilty. And this is exactly what he did a week later. "[In English] The SDA originally accepted the Cutileiro Agreement because it was a political game to secure the international recognition of a sovereign and independent Bosnia and Herzegovina, and because it would be responsible for the failure of the negotiations. The SDS, HDZ, and the European Community were in favour of BiH -- B and H remaining in its present borders but for its territories to be transformed." [Interpretation] Now, this is something that he found unacceptable, and on the 18th, 19th, he said, if This is deceit on the part of the Serbs, it is clear that they want to deceive the European Community, and they are to be blamed for the war. And now the gentleman admits that that's what they actually did, and that thereby they were the ones who wanted war. The Serb people and the Serb political parties accepted the minimum. We leave Yugoslavia. That is the most painful concession we could have made. The borders of Bosnia-Herzegovina remain as they are if internally we get our own constituent units. This is what Ambassador Cutileiro wrote in 1995, when the war was already over. This is what he wrote about what was being said about the Lisbon Agreement. This is what Ambassador Cutileiro wrote, and he felt that he should make this public to the world and that it was not that way, not quite as he had put it. This is his letter. "[In English] After several rounds of the talks -- of talks, our principles for constitutional arrangements for Bosnia and Herzegovina were agreed by all three parties (Muslim, Serbs and Croats) in Sarajevo on 18th of March, 1992. These continued -- this continued until the Muslims reneged on the agreement. Had they not done so, the Bosnian question might have been settled earlier with less loss of mainly Muslim life and land. To be fair, President Izetbegovic and his aides were encouraged to scupper the deal and to fight for a unitary Bosnian state by well-meaning outsiders who thought they knew better." [Interpretation] And this is the moment when we can also ask ourselves what could Karadzic or the SDS do, or all a million and a half Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina? They accepted everything. They accepted everything that was consistent with their survival. They accepted that their unit should be the worst, that it should be the one least to satisfy the interests and goals of the Serb people, but they accept it all and still they don't have a chance of preserving peace. The only thing that is expected of them, quite obviously, is what President Tudjman told the American delegation. He said the Serbs should leave Bosnia and not that the Muslims should leave Republika Srpska but Serbs out of Bosnia. That's what he said. I have to go back to the wedding party and the killing there and the barricades. They are mostly interpreted in a biased way by the Western media. They said that the barricades were set up because the Muslims voted for independence. That's just not true. It's not true. We didn't prevent that anywhere. And let's have another look at the ethnic map of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Let's see that again. Wherever you see blue is where we were in power, because that was the Serb majority, the blue. And nobody in that area could they have conducted a referendum had we decided against it. So we didn't prevent it. Therefore, it's not true that the barricades were set up because of the referendum. They were set up because of the killing, because a young man, who was a well-known criminal, by the way, understood that it was okay to shoot at a Serb wedding party and kill someone, and he was even celebrated by his ethnic community as hero. He wasn't arrested for a long time afterwards. And I think he was ultimately liquidated after the war, some three or four years ago in some cafe somewhere, but nobody took any steps to apprehend him at that time. So that was the 24th and 25th of March, when it was published that the SDA had withdrawn from the meeting. Now, on the 25th of March -- look at the rhythm, look at the tempo of this. We're no longer talking about a month or weeks as we were in Croatia. This is one shock after another, one day to the next. And we’ve now reached the 25th of March, where the armed forces of Croatia, the National Guards Corps, the MUP, whoever, you don't know who was active there, anyway, they transferred from Croatia to Bosnia-Herzegovina to Bosanski Brod where they met with illegal paramilitary units, led by Armin Pohara, who was the president of a party but he had some military formations too. They sang, they shot sporadically, and they killed a man and his son -- I think their name was Petrovic, at a petrol pump. There was no reason for it. They weren’t armed, and of course, those others were not allowed to shoot there, but when it came to shooting the Serbs, they went ahead and killed these two people. Nobody stood up to them, not the police of Bosnia-Herzegovina, not the Yugoslav People's Army who couldn't do anything about it because they were busy fighting in Croatia already, and they continued the next day, that is to say on the 26th of March, in the neighbouring village. Same thing happened as with the wedding party. Nobody stopped them and said, Hang on, what are you doing? On the 26 of March there was the slaughter of the Serbs in Sijekovac, and that poor village, Sijekovac, during World War II, well, a third of the population fled, a third of the population was killed, and a third was converted. Most of them converted back later, but some of them did not. Some remained Catholics. Now, the Serb side and this accused here was -- called up the people in the police saying, What's happening, who's going to save people? They said, We haven't got enough policemen. Why don't you recruit the reserve force? We can't without the minister. It was only the minister who was authorised to mobilise the reserve police force to go into action. Now, we asked them, We have the deputy minister, we have high-ranking officials in the ministry, we had Stanisic at the municipal level, we had Mandic at the republican level, so we asked Mandic and Repic, Why aren't you doing something to mobilise the reserve police force? And their answer was, We can't. Somebody has to order us to do that. There was nobody to issue the order. There was no barrier between the killers and the Serb people, Serb civilians. There was no barrier, and the Serb Assembly was to establish that barrier on the 27th of March, the day after the slaughter and 13 months after a far mightier body was set up by the SDA in February 1991 which was the National Security Council as an advisory body to the Assembly of the Serb people in Bosnia-Herzegovina. And the Prosecutor treats -- deals with that in paragraph 66 of its pre-trial brief. And that is how the paragraph reads. "[In English] The SNB was established by the Assembly on 27 March 1992, with Karadzic as its president. Although initially intended as an advisory body, the SNB in effect immediately turned into an executive organ resembling a central Bosnian Serb Crisis Staff and executing powers similar to those of the Presidency. Thus, as president of the SNB, Karadzic exercised authority over the Bosnian Serb state organs, that is, the Bosnian Serb forces and republican, regional, and municipal authorities. The SNB meeting in joint sessions with the Bosnian Serb government passed decision on strategic and military issues such as ordering the activation of the Crisis Staffs in certain conditions; appointing the acting commander of the Territorial Defence; defending Serb positions reached; and ordering a full mobilisation. Moreover, the SNB took important political decisions such as the appointment of ministers and the adoption of legislation." [Interpretation] Now, of course, the fact that the Prosecutor is summarising, this only happened actually when the war broke out. Until the war broke out, this body, the Council for National Security, was an advisory body, an advisory body, as the title says. And for want of any other body, any command or any formations, the Serb Assembly decided to have the Serbs in the police, that the Assembly should, through the advice of an advisory body, issue orders to the police to save the people. And the decision was taken on the 28th of February, had been taken that the Serb MUP be set up in conformity with the conference. However, it still had not been established and was still not working because it needed the agreement from -- of the other two sides to go ahead. Of course, in a paragraph the Prosecutor says that Stanisic and Mandic did that off their own bat. It's not got nothing to do with their volition. It was a decision taken by the Serb Assembly on the basis of the results of the conference on Bosnia-Herzegovina that was held in Lisbon under the Presidency of Ambassador Cutileiro, the presiding officer being Ambassador Cutileiro. Now we come to the 1st of April. Agreements and decisions are being made in the police force about the division of resources, the joint resources, and this was the distribution balance. The Prosecutor sees this as a criminal act, but it was quite normal where you have an entity split in two, an organisation split in two. You have to do the balance sheet to see what belongs to whom and who will get what in order to carry out the duty of keeping law and order. And agreements were reached in that respect and on that level. And on 1st of April, the Muslim extremists attacked Bijeljina. Not the Serb extremists, it was the Muslim extremists, and it was established here, through all the testimonies heard in this Tribunal, that somebody was riding a horse and he wanted to throw a bomb on a Serb cafe. There's no justification for that. They say that 10 or 12 days prior to that, the Serbs had caused an incident, a Serb had caused an incident in a Muslim cafe. However, the police arrested that Serb and sent him to Tuzla, to Muslim territory. They escorted him there and handed him over to the authorities. So there was no justification for this act. It came as orders from Sarajevo to make Bijeljina a problem, to problematise Bijeljina so that they could take over power and authority. The Prosecution says in its pre-trial brief "the forcible taking of Bijeljina by the Serbs," et cetera, et cetera, in one of the paragraphs of the indictment or pre-trial brief. That's completely absurd. It's absurd to say anything like that in view of the fact that Bijeljina municipality is predominantly Serb, and that the authorities were the Serb Democratic Party, and that everything was functioning property. I would just like at this point to go back a bit, backtrack to paragraph 66 that we read out, where the Prosecution says the following: That the council took over or had authority over Serb forces. Which Serb forces and which republican organs existed at that point in time? That's the question. Not a single one is the answer. There was the Assembly which was working as a joint Assembly and in a joint Assembly. There were no executive organs, none at all, nowhere. It was just not in the SAOs, nowhere. They were prepared in case of chaos, and especially Serb forces except for the Territorial Defence which existed in all the municipalities until the 20th of May, there were no Serb forces. The Prosecutor furthermore states that after the crisis, the crisis in Bijeljina lasted two days, so they call -- they say that Arkan was called in from Belgrade, and the Prosecutor, however, omits to say that there was a crisis and fighting in Bijeljina for a whole night, and that Arkan only arrived subsequently. Now, why did somebody call Arkan in? Because I don't justify this and I don't condemn it either. All I want to do is throw light on the truth. Sijekovac is some 100 kilometres away from Bijeljina and it was clear to one and all what had happened in Sijekovac, it was published, and what could the citizens of Bijeljina think but that they would suffer the same fate. And let me remind you and we have map about this and we will address that in due course if we have time. But by the 1st of April, let remind you, throughout Bosnia it was only the Serbs who were being killed. Whereas the Prosecutor for that period of time is holding me accountable and accusing me of pursuing a policy of warmongering, and we can see that on this map if we look at the border villages and the places in depth that were aflame. And it was exclusively against the Serbs that the barricades were set up in these areas. Check-points. Killings were taking place. People were being beaten up, intimidated. Exclusively the Serbs until the war broke out or, rather, the 1st of April. Now, the Prosecutor goes on to say that leading official Biljana Plavsic of the SDS went to Bijeljina. Well, I don't want to defend myself from things of that kind. It's just improper. Biljana Plavsic was in Bijeljina as a member of the state Presidency. It was a state delegation, not a party delegation, and it included Fikret Abdic, who was also not a member of the SDS. There was Jerko Doko, the minister of Defence, a Croat, who wasn't a member of the SDS either. So why was that the Prosecutor just focuses on Biljana Plavsic and notice her and not the members of the Presidency, the others ones, Abdic and so on? Well, it means that somebody's aiding and abetting the Prosecutor, that people assisting the Prosecutor are biased and helping the Prosecutor in that way. Biljana Plavsic was a state official there and it was a state delegation. On the 3rd of April we have the attack on Kupres. May we have the map back again, please. It was an attack launched by Croatian forces, local Croatian forces, and forces, regular forces from Croatia. An attack on Kupres. Kupres was a very sensitive area. You had 52 per cent Serbs, 40-odd per cent Muslims and 7 or 8 per cent -- or, rather, 40 per cent Croats and 8 per cent Muslims. So that is the largest flame that broke out, the largest flame on the map there, that's where Kupres is. For Croats in Central Bosnia this is significant because it is a mountain ridge linking Central Bosnia with Dalmatia and the coast, and that is where the fighting went on for several days, where the Serbs were slaughtered in Malovan, Vukovsko, and the villages around Kupres, and it was a terrible tremendous attack and tremendous suffering and fatalities on the part of the Serbs, but there was still not a war on. And the Serbs had nothing but the police to protect it them, whereas the police was not actually protecting them but working against them, and the Yugoslav People's Army that didn't have time with the situation. The Knin Corps appeared there which tried to protect the people in the region. Now on the 4th of April, the shocks didn't come every day, they came every hour. On the 4th of April Mr. Izetbegovic proclaimed general mobilisation. It is common knowledge -- it was common knowledge to him that the Serbs wouldn't respond because they knew what the police was doing. They knew what the Patriotic League was doing. They knew what the Green Berets were doing, and so the Serbs he knew would not join those units because they were afraid and it was their assumption that they would be killed. Karadzic calls up Izetbegovic and asks him to give up on the idea of mobilisation. That is a common -- that is common knowledge. Karadzic says, Why did you proclaim mobilisation? Nikola Koljevic and Biljana Plavsic was expressly against that. And he wasn't the president of Bosnia-Herzegovina; he was the president of the Presidency, therefore a collective Presidency. So he wasn't in a position to do that and I told him that publicly, and we have the footage of this, the OTP has it too. We -- I say it's madness. The people are armed. Nobody is able to control the armament of the people anymore, and now you're proclaiming general mobilisation to legalise rifles which people are secreting. That is tantamount to a declaration of war, and we have footage of that too, so we won’t waste any time now. We will screen it in due course during the trial. And on the 5th of April, I state that it was a mistake to go ahead with -- that was a mistake. Recognition should be delayed, the conference should have been speeded up, and then we would have had peace. Instead of that, what was accelerated was recognition and the conference was slowed down. That was a recipe for war. On the 5th of April, in the morning, the apartment of my family was bullet-ridden, with a machine-gun, and we have witnesses to bear out the fact that they were waiting to kill us but we were all downstairs, but always -- already in the Holiday Inn, the party offices, and they failed to kill us. On the 5th of April, Izetbegovic, Kljujic, and I left -- or was it Brkic, I don't remember. Anyway, we went to the television station with General Kukanjac to appeal for peace. At the same time, a day before, the Serb MUP was given agreement that the headquarters of the MUP should be in the school of the Ministry of the Interior at Vraca, above Grbavica. So on that April the 5th, while we were broadcasting over television, the Serb MUP which came to take up its offices was held in ambush, and two wonderful young Specials, Serbs, were killed. The other 30 men who came to help them take up their premises, they were -- they captured 140 Muslims and 400 of the pupils, but not a hair of their head was harmed; whereas these wonderful two young Serb men were killed. On the 5th and 6th of April, on the 5th of April in the evening, terror broke lose in Sarajevo. It was the worst night ever. There were snipers in all the high-rise buildings, Green Beret snipers. A policeman was killed in the joint police station - his name was Petrovic - by them, and it was terrible to be a Serb that night in Sarajevo. The Serbs withdrew to their own districts and areas and tried to defend those districts and their families and the people living in them, and that is how the line dividing the town was established. It wasn't a siege, a line of siege, but it was a line separating and dividing two parts of the town. Now, in the Milosevic trial, witness Eve-Anne Prentice, from Britain, confirmed -- she confirmed that it wasn't a city under siege, it was a city divided. And George Kenney from the State Department, who was well acquainted about our situation, said on his own initiative, without having to be asked by the Prosecution or the Defence, said that it was wrong to state that Sarajevo was a city under siege like Leningrad. Sarajevo was a divided city like Beirut, with one section of the population living in one area and the other in the other. In Beirut it was common knowledge that after the working hours, at 3.00, shooting broke out; whereas by 3.00 p.m. everybody was at work. On the 12th of April, Ambassador Cutileiro arrives, and at that time Vance was also in Sarajevo. We signed an agreement on truce with Mr. Cutileiro. During the talks with Mr. Cutileiro and Cyrus Vance, we established that we had to accelerate the defining of these three constituent units because that could have stopped war. So if anyone knew that their village was going to be in a certain constituent unit, they didn't have any need to fight. However, on the afternoon of that same day, Hasan Efendic, the then commander of their Territorial Defence, issued the well-known directive for immediate combat readiness which, translated, meant an attack on all possible Serbian and Yugoslav People’s Army targets, and Bosnian Serb targets. On the 22nd of April, this accused announced and offered his platform for the cessation of hostilities and the continuation of seeking for a political solution. This is a very important moment, and during this trial we shall see that this was the position of the Serbian side which were contained in documents. The Serbian positions were expressed in the Serbian Assembly. There was a provision that a deputy cannot be held accountable for his speech. However, an Assembly is not there for people to deliver speeches but, rather, to legislate, to adopt resolutions, declarations, decisions, conclusions, and recommendations. So at least seven documents of that type were produced by the Assembly, and an instrument for producing this kind of documents is free debate. The OTP said that an enraged or angry deputy that was affected by something during the war had said something in the Assembly, and they say that Karadzic didn't warn him and caution him. The president didn't have to be present in the Assembly. I was there often but not always, and particularly the president is not a teacher who should discipline the deputies. A deputy is a directly elected official, just like the president, and I had no right to do this. However, if I saw that this could affect some legislature or the constitution or some other decision, then I intervened and tried to have an impact on the final outcome. In addition to thousands of documents officially adopted by the Assembly, published in the Official Gazette, the OTP couldn't find a single document to charge me with or to lay blame on me for it, even though it was a legislative body. I was not responsible for that body. I was only responsible to the extent that I may once send back to the Assembly the documents that are submitted to me for my signature. And if they are adopted, then I must sign them. That means the President’s hands are tied – he does not have unlimited power, though he be Karadzic himself. Among all these laws, decrees, and other documents that were adopted, the OTP did not rely on a single one that could have held this accused accountable for any breach of domestic legislature or any international instrument of international law. So this was the course of events that led to war between the 12th, when the elections were held. Let us look briefly at paragraph 78 of the pre-trial brief where it says: "[In English] Even before its inaugural session, Karadzic and the leadership planned that the Assembly would have a role in the acquisition of Serbian-claimed territories." [Interpretation] So on the 24th of October, when we walked out of the Assembly and decided to form our own Assembly in order to exert pressure on the SDA to give up on their war plans, the OTP says, no, no, they establish this -- but this was in October 1991. They established this Assembly to serve as an instrument for capturing territories. Can we please now look at the map again. The ethnic map. What territories were Serbs allegedly to capture? Those were already their territories. If you look at the front lines, you will see that -- [In English] Can we -- can we have a map. [Interpretation] Of these Serb territories held by them for centuries, the Serbs were prepared for the sake of peace to give up on some of them. You can see how it looks like without front lines, but now you're going to see how it looked like with the front lines. The OTP claimed that on the 24th of October we established our own Assembly in order to -- can we have it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You have to turn on the ELMO or video.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you can see the same map. The Serbian forces, the Serbian people, the Territorial Defence - according to the law, every municipality had Territorial Defence. The president of the municipality was commander of the TO. Tito's doctrine of an armed people must be clarified here. It explains many things that would otherwise remain unexplained, if we were to consider that Bosnia and Yugoslavia, like other countries, had their own armed forces, highly trained and kept under command and control. And these were people who went to the edges of their own territories in order to prevent slaughter. These were the front lines throughout the entire war. If you look at the central part, Your Excellencies, if we had advanced further on we would have benefitted from that, because we would have shortened the front lines and increased the deployment of our forces and include our reserve forces. However, if the Muslim and Croat forces advanced, they would have stretched their front and would have been weakened. So from the strategic point of view, if we had advanced, we could have been more strong. We could have been stronger and we could have captured the whole of Bosnia. And you will see this with regard to Sarajevo in particular. Now, what the OTP claims about our Assembly being established to prevent any violation of the constitution, they say that this was created in order to take over the territories that were already ours. We never left our own ethnic territories. And the fact that there were Muslims in Prijedor and Eastern Bosnia, wherever there were 20 or 30.000 Serbs and -- or Muslims or Croats, this could have become a canton without war. So I have to defend myself from the allegations that we didn't have enough power on the 24th of October, or the 27th March, or the 6th of April, because we had our own forces only on the 20th of May, not counting the Territorial Defence. The Territorial Defence existed in every enterprise, in every company. That was the concept of an armed people. We have a situation different than in the rest of the world, and in order for you to understand that, you should know that even every company had their own territorial unit and its weapons, and that particularly applied to municipalities. Your Excellency, I don't know if I managed to portray for you this horrible course of events against the Serbs who constituted one-third, who were not organised in any respect other than having its own Assembly and its deputies who were partly performing in the joint Assembly and partly trying to protect the Serbian people from their own state, from the police, from the state-sponsored terror of their own country. Now let us see what the police was doing. Why did the SDS ask Ambassador Cutileiro for the constituent unit to have their own police forces? Everywhere in the world the police forces are decentralised all the way down to the level of municipality. In the US, you have city and district police forces, and there are state police forces, and then you have federal police forces, and this is what we were asking for. Let us just see what this police did. I'm talking about the joint police in which we had our representatives and our own positions won at democratic elections. At the very beginning, the joint police forces set out to effect Muslim supremacy and the SDA, the government organs, the police, and the Green Berets and the police became almost one and were equal to one another, and all of that was under the command of the SDA. The number one man in the joint police of Bosnia-Herzegovina was a cleric, Hasan Cengic, who was not a member of the police. For example, on the 11th of July, 1991, while we were in negotiations with Zulfikarpasic and Filipovic about the historic Serbian-Muslim agreement supported by Izetbegovic: "[In English] The SDA -- on 11th of July, 1991, the SDA issued instructions for sending candidates of the MUP educational centre in Croatia," and this instruction is number 12583 in 1991. [Interpretation] What is this all about? In see secrecy, behind the back of the Serb deputy minister, Mr. Stanisic, and Mr. Stanisic who was chief of police for Sarajevo, preparations were made to send groups of policemen to Croatia who was at the time fighting against Yugoslavia. They were being sent to undergo training so that they can repeat the same activities that Croatia pursued. You can also see a lot of indications of what they did. Hasan Cengic, his father, Halid Cengic, established the first forerunner of the Patriotic League - the first armed unit in Foca, in August 1990, before the elections. Hasan Cengic – a true son of his father - took control of the joint police force: "[In English] In accordance with the agreement between officials of the Bosnian and Croatian police MUP, and pursuant to the instructions regarding the employment of police candidates as the Croatian and MUP educational centre, the SDA recommends the above-mentioned candidates for the course at your centre." [Interpretation] This is a cover letter sent with a list of Muslim policemen who were to be trained in Zagreb secretly. This cover letter was not signed by anyone from the police, but, rather, by a person from the SDA, and this is the proof that there was a complete merger between the SDA and the Muslim part of the police. So this is how this joint MUP looks like, and there was a reason good enough for us to leave the police but this wasn't done until 1991. The police is intercepting politicians' conversations, private conversations of ordinary citizens, et cetera. We are going to see a lot of intercepts of that kind. I'm not concerned about that at all. They are going to be very helpful to see what was done at the time. I recently asked to be provided with intercepts of conversations between Izetbegovic, Ganic, and others. I naively suppose that if they listened in to everybody's conversation I could have them, but it turns out the only ones who were -- whose telephones were tapped were the Serbs. So until that moment the SDA established -- [In English] The SDA established its military wing, the so-called Patriotic League. SDA armed the Patriotic League. SDA obstructed the appointments of SDS personnel in the MUP, of Serbian personnel in the MUP. SDA replaced a large number of Serbian employees in the Bosnian MUP. SDA sent Muslim police personnel to the Croatian MUP for military training [Interpretation] That was at the time when Croatia was in war with Yugoslavia. [In English] SDA carried out an illegal mobilisation of the reserve forces for Bosnian MUP. SDA illegally intercepted telephone conversations of the Serbian leadership. [Interpretation] And they did a lot of other things but these are the most striking ones, describing what our government partners were doing without any core decisions, and they shouldn't have done that without proper core decisions. Needless to say that the SDS and the entire Serbian nation knew about all this, but without a smoking gun and without solid proof there was no way to disclose that. And even when that was divulged, this was refuted immediately and the Serbian side was accused of corrupting inter-ethnic relations and raising tensions. This is one conversation between the accused and the deputy minister, who was a Serb but not a member of the SDS, but he was nominated by the Serbs to protect the Serbian interest and to be part of the checks and balances. Let's hear it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: "Karadzic: Alija can only made a decision to call upon the Muslims to join the Territorial Defence, and some people around him are ready to start the war. We know that quite well. They are preparing a war, they organised the Main Staff, you don't know that, where the staff is. There is a huge number of armed people. There are preparations for war. There are drills to block barracks. There are counter-manoeuvres of the army and here they are going for war. They want the unlawful way although we've proved to them that they cannot legally or politically carry that out. We've told them to use the constitutional procedure to change the constitution but they don't want to because they don't they know they stand a chance with international public. They don't stand a chance within the legal system. The only chance they've got is to try and trick us, but the Serbs won't allow that "Zepinic: Izetbegovic is getting a chance to achieve what no one has ever achieved. That is to establish an Islamic state in Europe. "Karadzic: We don’t stand a chance. Europe, they know what it is. They don't need us. They would make the state without us, but Europe would not recognise an Islamic -- that is, a Muslim state at all, and that's a big problem for them. They are trying to make us their hostages, hostages of their state." That was the 17th of June, 1991, my conversation with our top representative in the police force who will come here to confirm this, although there's really no need to have this confirmed I believe that there is no need for me to go on about the MUP any longer. It's time for the break anyway, isn't it? The MUP was then the strongest support of the SDA policy anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellency, is it the right time to take the break now? I can go on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, we'll take a break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are the further contacts between this accused person and the highest positioned Serb in the police, who is not a member of the SDS, of course. He is an expert, a police expert. And we see that this accused says: "We've been tricked at the MUP especially at the state security. Please don't let them not know. Nothing should be done single-handedly. This is not a private thing. The entire collegium should meet and they should be told: This position is vacant and we suggest this man for the job. I beg you to stop doing these things in a private basis." I'd like to draw your attention to what the president of the ruling party is saying here. It's not that he is saying that they should listen to him. It's the Serbs at the MUP who say, "We don't want you to impose some Serb on us. We want to be the ones who are going to say which Serb deserves to be in that position." So it's not being done by Radovan Karadzic. It's Radovan Karadzic who is asking members of the police to defend their own people by putting professionals in the right positions. They, not the political party. And then we go on, on the 22nd of July, what I read out just now was on the 8th, this is the 22nd of July: "Tell them not to play games. Look, they're in Prijedor in the afternoon, Friday afternoon. They positioned a man there. The Muslim is a chief, the chief of defence is a Muslim, and the chief of the Territorial Defence is a Muslim, and the commander should have been ours." That was one of the routine manipulations. The Serbs get a particular position, and they don't allow it to happen, or they put a Muslim as deputy. But you see what the scenario is, for bloodshed in Prijedor that will eventually happen and we will see how. Let's move on. September, the 17th of September, 1991, Karadzic, Plavsic: "Today we'll probably talk to them," the Muslims, that is, "and I'll say no talks until they stop deciding in MUP where each Serb is going to work. Until they stop making decisions for us. We'll separate our part of the MUP there. We'll divide the MUP into cantons. You should know that we'll do that. They are proving to us how we are going to live here," in that state that is. Excellencies, these were the shocks that we had to deal with, not on a weekly or a monthly basis like in Croatia, but on an hourly basis. Now, this is the accused talking to the chief of the political party in Bosanska Krajina, Dr. Vukic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Karadzic: There are forces in Bosnia and Herzegovina who know what they cannot achieve what they want without a war, and they need a reason for starting war so they could blame someone else. We must not give them the reason to start the war, and that's the most essential thing. By the way, both the international and our constitutional laws are on our side."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, I think it's clear. Izetbegovic wants to wage war. Babic is playing into his hands. I mean, playing into the hands of warmongering Izetbegovic, and this reference is to the late Milan Babic who was in Krajina often because it was close to him. And as you will see during the trial he visited and that was very difficult for us. We had to put out the fire every time he went there. Babic is playing right into the hands of this warmonger Izetbegovic: "You tell our people from Krajina that I said to Alija Izetbegovic that he is preparing a war and that he is seeking assistance for a war. Please give him this answer of ours. Tell him there are forces in Bosnia that know that there cannot be a war if it doesn't come from above, and they need a pretext for war. They want to blame someone else. We should not give a pretext for war. That is the most important thing. International law and humanitarian law are on our side. The basic thing is that we shouldn't do anything that should be a pretext for war."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] The Muslims are strongly turning against Alija's war intentions. They have a republic. They have Yugoslavia. No one sane will go to war. Alija would like to go to war to change that, and now Alija cannot explain to the Muslim people why he would go to war. The only thing that he needs now is an alibi for a war. We should not help him achieve that."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a conversation between Professor Koljevic, member of the Presidency, and Karadzic, where we say that our –- irresponsible people should not make silly statements. They won't do anything else. We –- that they shouldn't do anything that would be taken as an alibi for waging war. So, we were working even on that level to make sure war would be avoided. And now let us look at paragraphs 109 and 110 of the Prosecution pre-trial brief. This is how these two paragraphs treat the accused in relation to the MUP. "[In English] From the outset of the conflict, the MUP played a significant role in establishing and maintaining Bosnian Serb authority over the territory and in implementing the common criminal purpose. Following the take-overs, the MUP took a lead role in disarming, arresting, rounding up, detaining, beating, killings, and expelling Muslims and Croats. "For months prior its division, Karadzic contemplated the division of the MUP as an essential component of the division of B and H and the realisation of the final goal 'to break off with Muslims and Croats forever.'" [Interpretation] Well, that's what the Prosecution says about Karadzic and Karadzic's wishes and intentions to create a MUP just like that and in this way break up this idyll between the Muslims and the Serbs. And the Prosecution is actually trying to reconstruct Serb intentions, as it were, on the basis of Serb behaviour. Serb behaviour is a response. It's a reaction. It is impermissible, it is impossible to say that that is intention rather than reaction. The SDA decides what the Serbs are going to do. It's not the Serbs who are deciding that, and that's the way it was throughout. From February 1991, after the elections, the Serbs' hand was forced, if I can put it that way, and we have to react to what they do, otherwise we will go down the drain. Now let us look at our efforts to have a police. We actually asked the European Community for constituent units to have their respective police forces. This is an excerpt from the Lisbon Agreement -- or, rather, the Cutileiro Plan. [In English] "The statement of principles for new constitutional arrangements for Bosnia and Herzegovina. "(D) The constituent units. "The civil service, the police, and the local judiciary and any national guard established by a constituent unit would reflect proportionally the national composition of the constituent unit." [Interpretation] From Ambassador Cutileiro and the European Community we got the right to our own police force. It was only then, on the 28th of February, that we decided, the Assembly decided that we would have our own police force, but we did not establish it before the 1st of April. So our hand was forced, but nevertheless, the Prosecution charges me that I did this in a premeditated fashion with the intention of achieving something at some point in time. Instead of clearly seeing that this was caused by SDA behaviour. Throughout that time, we were aware of the secret agreement between Kucan, Tudjman, and Izetbegovic to go to war and we are aware of the information to the effect that Izetbegovic was asked, in the second half of 1991, why he did not go to war with Yugoslavia. And he says, I will, I will, but I'm just waiting for the right moment, that is the moment when he is given encouragement. And from mid-October onwards, he does away with any possible solution for a peace -- a peaceful settlement. The OTP has a few cornerstones upon which they would like to construct Serb guilt and Serb responsibility. One of the things that the OTP charges me with is the paper versions Variant A and B. Unfortunately, that was not created within the SDS. We did not discuss it. We did not adopt it. And there are no traces of any such thing, and if that had happened, there would have been traces because of all our transcripts were seized. Old officers, pensioned officers, when they realised what Martin Spegelj recommended to Croats, You go to one apartment, dum, dum, and you shoot him in the stomach, et cetera, et cetera. When they saw that in Sarajevo their apartments were being marked and that an assassin may ring their doorbell and, bang, shoot them in the stomach, they therefore prepared some guidelines as to what should be done in order to prevent a war from happening, that kind of thing from happening. There is no political party and no person like Karadzic who could do anything about it if there is chaos. No one knows what they are going to do. So now let us see what this paper that I referred to says. Paragraph 36: "[In English] On or about 20th of December, 1992, at a meeting in the Holiday Inn in Sarajevo, Karadzic distributed to the municipality leaders instructions for the establishment of clandestine bodies, the Serbian Crisis Staffs (A/B). The confidential instructions established the bodies that would be among the primary instruments through which Karadzic and other members of BSL asserted control over territories and removed non-Serbs." [Interpretation] Look at what it says in this piece of paper. It's the pensioned officers who actually provided this: "In the implementation of all these measures ensure the respect for the national and other rights of members of all peoples and subsequently ensure their involvement in the administrative authorities to be set up by the Assembly of the Serb people in the municipality." Again we have to view all of this in the context of the conference, the Lisbon conference and the Cutileiro Plan. We know that the SDA is going to try to derogate it by way of war. This was envisaged to avoid war and to avoid chaos, and to preserve the heritage of the conference and to keep people out of harm's way. There is no need to emphasise to what extent the interests of others are being taken into account, especially by these officers who were in favour of brotherhood and unit anyway. The other cornerstone of the OTP are strategic objectives. Strategic objectives were not adopted. As a matter of fact, they were just stated to the Assembly on the 12th of May, that they would be the platform for the conference. When it was clear that there would be a war and that we would elect a Presidency, a Presidency was indeed elected, and two members of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mrs. Biljana Plavsic and Mr. Nikola Koljevic, and the third one was yours truly, elected to the Presidency by the Assembly. We then stated what our position would be vis-a-vis the European Community in continuing our efforts to resolve the crisis through peaceful means. Since there was a war on, we could no longer have enclaves on a discontinuous basis because people would not dare live there. Something changed in the objectives -- or, rather, our position changed vis-a-vis the negotiations with the European Community. A month later, in June or July, the Presidency made a decision. The strategic objectives were not made public yet, but then a decision was made to make them public and to send them to the European Community -- or, rather, the negotiators, together with the map. So this is no secret document, secret piece of paper. This is the terribly unfair judgement against Krajisnik. This is what it says with regard to this matter: "It would be incorrect to place these goals on a pedestal, as the Prosecution does, for in the final analysis they are anodyne statements serving as official state policy and even qualifying for a publication in the Bosnian Serb Republic's Official Gazette. If one is inclined to find them -- to find in them insidious hidden meanings, it is because of the context and the events that followed. An anachronistic reading of the May goals is not only inadvisable, it misses the point. Just as an anachronistic reading of the December instructions," that's Variants A and B, "misses the point. The instructions and the goals lacked substance and utility, but they did symbolise a new central authority at a time when the old order had disintegrated." This Chamber shows that we are right to reorganise when the old system was collapsing and parts of this disintegrated system are flying at us with the aim of destroying us. So this paragraph deals with two cornerstones in the indictment against me and it -- as far as both of them are concerned, the Prosecution is not right, but although this judgement was made earlier and in the final judgement this was not appealed, the Prosecution still maintains that it could use this against me. Now let's see, to wind up this area, how Lord Owen sees the situation who came to the Bosnia negotiations very anti-Serb in sentiment because he had the wrong information given to him, and he was soon to be surprised, as were indeed other people from the United Nations who came and thought the Serbs were brutal, but after a month or two they saw what was really going on. This is what Lord Owen says in his book "Balkan Odyssey." "The image of unarmed Bosnian Muslims was not changed even when Alija Izetbegovic openly admitted on television that the Bosnian government had smuggled weapons through secret channels: 30.000 rifles and machine-guns, 20 million bullets, 37.000 mines, 4.600 antitank rockets, 20.000 grenades, 90.000 uniforms, and 12.000 boots." And I should like to add to that, from the Muslim sources in Sarajevo there were 80.000 mines produced. That is their confirmation. In that same Sarajevo which was allegedly under siege and mistreated by the Serb army, they had a factory in which they manufactured 80.000 mortars and mines. And the -- but the Prosecution persists. On the basis of our reactions, panic and in defence, is trying to construe this and present it as being something that we had planned a long time ago; whereas in actual fact we were responding to the challenges of Hasan Cengic and others, the ones they laid in our path, according to the Islamic Declaration as a pretext for chaos, because they said, We can't wait for natural pretexts and causes, we must construct our own. Now, the SDS -- how would the Serbs, the SDS, under regular conditions have reacted and regular conditions would have been secured by the acceptance of new agreements, which the Serbs offered or accepted if they had been made by others. What would have happened in those regular circumstances? How could they have thought of, let alone planned, separating parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina that they considered to be Serbian? The Prosecution skips over that and asks the following question: how did the SDS dare engage in the said activities, when it was impossible to do this peacefully due to the ethnic mixture? Now, this ethnic mixture is true for the SDA too. They, too, did not dare and should not have engaged in forcible secession from Yugoslavia because we are so ethnically mixed. So we were not in favour of stepping down from Yugoslavia, stepping out from Yugoslavia, but if they left Yugoslavia, and took us out with them too, then we wanted to secure our positions in Bosnia, as we're all a mixed-up population there, you see. Now we have a well-known session held on the 24th of January, and this accused is advocating that the agreement with Cengic about regionalisation should be accepted. It could have been done within a fortnight, by the end of January, and at the end of February there's a referendum. And here's what I say: I say that I and all of us can now imagine what would have happen, gentlemen, if, God forbid, unrest were to break out between the ethnic groups and have a religious war in Bosnia-Herzegovina. And we can draw it on the board. The Serbs would flee from Muslim areas, and the Muslims from Serb areas. The Croats would go to their own regions. There would be a lot of shooting along the way. Cities would tumble. There would be bloodshed up to our knees. And where would we be then? The same place we are now. The Serbs in Serb regions, the Muslims in Muslim regions, and the Croats in Croatian regions, homogenous. And what need we do then? We would once again have to sit down to the negotiating table and to put three signatures to an agreement, because without three signatures to an agreement there's no solution to Bosnia-Herzegovina. And here's the proof of it: On the 24th of January this accused here says it is clear to one and all, and it was clear to him, too, that there was no fait accompli, but -- and we're talking about January 1992, a month before the referendum. Now, where is this common criminal purpose or joint criminal enterprise that this accused stands accused of along with his associates? Where is it? When we say: "We are going to have this and this. Unless we reach an agreement, we will have such and such." We don’t want that. And there's another portion where this accused says: "Let us avoid having the situation slip out of our control. We are the ones who control order. We cannot bridle chaos." So those are matters which guided us the -- in seeking from Cutileiro to enable us to have our police force, and it was accepted. Now, I'd like to draw your attention to the following. Let's take a look at Sarajevo itself. This is the broader area around Sarajevo. The green line is -- or, rather, the blue line is the Serbs, and where it says "HVO," that area there, on the one hand -- facing us we have the HVO, on the other side we have the Muslims and then there's us. So we are being encircled by them. We are under their siege. May I be allowed to get up to show you this on the map. This is the Sarajevo area, broader area. We'll explain this later on, but these are Serb territories and they're under Serb control. Not all of them but some of them are. Now, part of the Serb territory is surrounded by Croatian and Muslim forces. So we are also under siege. This is the city proper, and we have a divided town, and you'll see why the Serbs are around Sarajevo, located around Sarajevo. Let's go back to the ethnic map -- or, rather, let's have the ethnic map of Sarajevo put up on our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was compiled by the same institute as the Bosnia map earlier on, but this is the city of Sarajevo, and you can see the borders. The white -- thin white line is the city proper, the inner city. The blue are the settlements and districts where the Serbs were in a significant majority, and the light blue areas where they were a relative majority. So this was the city of Sarajevo, entirely Serb. As you can see, it was the property of the Pavlovic family, the squires. When the Turks arrived, the family was destroyed, but the Serbs remained living in and around Sarajevo, and for a long time they were the majority population in Sarajevo. When the war broke out, the Serbs managed to protect this area in the centre of town. May we zoom into that and see the front line there. I can't see that on my screen. Do I have it? Now we can see that the Serbs have succeeded in protecting part of town, and it's the well-known settlement -- Serb settlement of Grbavica on the left bank of the Miljacka River. On the right bank, Pofalici, a Serb settlement, was one they did not succeed in defending, and by 15 May there was not a single house standing, nor a single person left alive there. More than 250 people were killed, in the middle of the city and well within the range of Mr. Izetbegovic’s authorities. Mladic's house was there as well. Luckily his family managed to escape but the whole area was destroyed. Now, Your Excellencies, take a look at this. The Serbs here are only controlling their own parts, their own parts of town, that's all. The city proper and the surrounding parts. And those Serb territories are located under a Muslim siege, surrounded by Muslim forces, the Muslim-Croatian Army. Now I'd like to ask you to focus on the Hadzici municipality in the lower left-hand corner. Can we zoom into the Hadzici, please. It's on the other map, the left-hand corner. The Prosecutor says that the Serbs took over control of Hadzici, where they were in the minority. It was true that we were the minority, but all this green area to the very left, to the extreme left, is Hadzici municipality which the Serbs were not in control of. The Serbs only controlled the Serbian part of Hadzici. And throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina, wherever they say or write that the Serbs had assumed control over such and such a municipality in which they were a minority, that is just not true. It's not correct. All the Serbs were in control of was the Serb portion of the municipalities. Then it says "Hrasnica" down there, number 5. Number 5 is Hrasnica. Half of Hrasnica is half of Ilidza municipality. The Serbs only controlled the Serb half of that municipality, the Ilidza municipality. They never attempted to take control of Hrasnica. Can you see that? I think you can see number 5. Number 5 is Hrasnica on this map. And opposite Hrasnica to the right is Lukavica, Dobrinja, and so on and so forth. So in actual fact we didn't control any Muslim settlement nor did we attempt do so; whereas the Muslims did control significant Serb areas, and nobody remained alive there in mid-May. The people had to flee those regions. Now, the truth set in stone or marble that Sarajevo wasn't under a siege is true. The truth of it is it was a divided city, both the city proper and the area around it. And on this map we can see the city proper, and we see the front lines, which are being held at 100 to 200 metres between each other, and sometimes the distance between them is just 15 metres. Sometimes in one flat you have the Muslims, in the next you have the Serbs. And the front line runs right through the building. I would like to be allowed to get up again and approach the screen so that I can explain this to you using the map. This is my city. I've spent 50 years of my life living in it. This is Grbavica. This is the Miljacka River going across this area. The Serbs protected Grbavica because it was a majority population over there.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused kindly be provided with a microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, could you start again with your microphone on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we see the front line, and the front line follows along and stretches -- well, the two lines run alongside each other. The red line contains the Muslim and Serb front line. We are adjacent to each other there. And when somebody says a Serb shell, and you will hear from Prosecution witnesses, all they can say is the direction the shell came from.
