Now, who's going to say, if you look at this, what were legitimate targets in this area, in the old part of town? What were the legitimate targets that the Serb side had the right to respond to? I'd like to ask you to focus on this area. We still don't have the entire map and we will in due course when the trial gets going, but look at all the schools and nurseries that were transferred into military premises, turned into military premises. The nursery called Pcelica, kindergarten Pcelica, in the Svetozar Markovic area, it was the command post of the 105th Brigade, a Military Police battalion. In a kindergarten, mark you. So that is the city that was helpless and innocent, and there were always three times more soldiers than in the Serbian Romanija Corps. They always had three times the manpower that we did. Here you have the command post of the 105th Mountain Brigade, as I said, the Razija Omanovic primary school this time. This is the old city core, the old part of town called Bascarsija, dating back to Turkish times, and we're being shot at from there, and we're suffering losses. And you'll be able to see that there were also mortars on this bank over here, above the brewery, which were most probably used to shoot at Markale, because that's the general axis, the direction from which the shells are coming towards that part of town. I think that you have that in the lists, that that is listed. It's somewhere around there, in the Bistrik area. Fire positions, Bistrik area, Bistrik street, mortars, a battery of mortars. So it's a slope facing town, facing their positions. We were behind them and -- to the south. And if you hold that position you can shoot at any part of town whenever you feel like it. Now look at this very narrow part of town. How many legitimate targets there are. This -- these are 10 per cent of the legitimate targets that were -- 10 per cent of what we're going to show as being legitimate targets, but we are going to show the abuse of hospitals, schools, kindergartens turned into military facilities. Here we have the command of the 152nd Mountain Brigade which is a foreign language school in Vaso Miskin Street. It's been renamed now but it's the same street where there was that explosion in the bread line on the 27th of May, 1992. Here we have the command post of the military police. Here we have Bascarsija, the Old Town centre. And downstream from there, to the left -- could you zoom in to the left. Can we move to Skenderija, opposite Skenderija. There we have Dositejeva Street. Pan left. Pan left a bit more. Upstream. Here we have the command post of the 105th, and it's the Sipad building, a civilian facility turned into a military facility. And if, from a flat roof of that building, they shot at us and we returned fire, they would portray this as nonselective shelling of the town by the Serb army. This is a logistics base on the Dositejeva Street, now called Branislava Djurdjeva number 2. This is a helicopter fleet in the centre of Sarajevo. This is a first-rate legitimate military target. Here we see Marin Dvor, which is in the Old Town. Immediately next to it is Holiday Inn hotel where foreign journalists were residing. And around this area was the stage of all these stage-managed events and shells. For example, if you look at the Catholic cathedral, this was the logistics base of the 105th Mountain Brigade. Right next to the church. This is the street that leads to Vrbanja bridge. There's a firing position, a mortar firing position on -- at the corner of this street. So you see these firing positions in the centre of the town. Also, 12.7 was a submachine -- or machine-gun nest in the centre of the town. This is a sniper position at the corner of the streets Gundulica and Branimira Cosica. Now we're going to see how many schools and kindergartens were used -- abused. This is a faculty near Vrbanja, and that's what we see a minute ago. Now, the museum building had a firing position as well in it. We were being shot from that position, and we had to respond, and we were accused of firing at the museum. 12.7. So if we are attacking this position, we were accused of firing indiscriminately at Sarajevo. There is a footage where Mladic says, "Turn the weapons at Velesici. There no Serbs there." But the one firing knows what the targets are. The targets are legitimate targets, because we know that there were legitimate targets in Velesici. It was a firing position of the 101st, Centrotrans Buca Potok, and there was a maintenance repair shop for armored vehicles. Now, the building of the transport institute, which was another legitimate target, this is a forward command post in Velesici, in the auto repair shop. And when Mladic says, "Target Velesici," he is not referring to civilian facilities. He is referring to legitimate targets. On the other hand, the OTP thinks that although we know what it was all about we had to say a false sentence, fire at the car repair shop in Velesici which is the command post. This is not how this is being done. The Kosevo Hospital now, the OTP witnesses are going to confirm that they riddled it with bullets from their own weapons, and this is a legitimate target in the yard of the Kosevo Hospital which belonged to the 105th Brigade. Now, this is the physical education faculty which is a university facility also abused, and there's another faculty building of the civil engineering which was occupied by the 105th Brigade. The Vuk Karadzic elementary school. I don't believe it's call that any longer. Karadzic was an ancestor of mine who was born in Serbia who carried out the reform of the Serbian culture and Serbian alphabet. I think this was enough. Now, I would like to enumerate for you things that can be said with relation to Sarajevo. So overall, Sarajevo was build on the Serb-owned land. For a long time it was populated by majority of Serbs. All the settlements around Sarajevo, and some of its neighbourhoods have always been majority Serb. Some quarters in the city centre had a Serb majority before the war, and before the Second World War, all of Sarajevo, and some neighbourhoods in particular, were almost 100 per cent Serb. Before the breakout of this war and with regard to the conference on Bosnia- Herzegovina, the Serbian side did not propose a division, but a transformation of the town, on the model of Brussels. We were saying that Bosnia and Herzegovina should be reorganized like Switzerland. This meant cantonization after the Swiss model. For Sarajevo, not division, but transformation similar to the one carried out in Brussels. As you know, there are 17 boroughs in Brussels. None of them are mixed. They're either Flemish or Walloon. That is how conflicts are avoided. But yet it is only the Balkan peoples who are being asked to try to live in a melting pot that will be pregnant with needless anxiety and tensions and conflicts. So, the request was to transform Sarajevo so that each community had its own borough and thus to remove at least one of the reasons for tensions. This precludes any intention of terrorising the town. Your Excellencies, in the map that you saw, we didn't have professional army. These were the people living 50 metres from the front line. They had nowhere to escape. They had to fight 50 metres from their own home. They were sleeping in their homes. They were not billeted in barracks. These were people's army. They had to fight for Sarajevo. Had the war been avoided, Sarajevo would have been transformed into several municipalities, and each municipality would take care of its own affairs. The so-called gerrymandering was carried out in the whole of Bosnia-Herzegovina, including Sarajevo. Gerry Mander [sic] was a master of election manipulation. He managed to establish such constituencies so that weaker parties would win the elections, and this phenomenon of gerrymandering was very much present in Bosnia-Herzegovina. For example, Hrasnica was attached to Ilidza so that the Serbs would not have their own municipality. Rajlovac, the place where Mr. Krajisnik hailed, used to be a municipality, was attached to Novi Grad where Serbs became a minority, and any development of Rajlovac was halted. We are going to demonstrate to you this gerrymandering process applied in the whole of Bosnia which rendered Serbian areas totally devastated. So the plan for Sarajevo was to be reorganised administratively, and it was necessary anyway to make smaller municipalities. Previously there were enormous municipalities and nobody could do anything without resorting to bribe. Even without the war and without the crisis this should have been done. Sarajevo was composed of ten municipalities before the war. The Serbs only had control in Serbian municipalities, and in Muslim majority municipalities, they only controlled Serbian neighbourhoods. If we can have back the map with the front line. I have it on my screen. Yes. To the far left is Pale, and this is Renovica. The Muslim municipality of Pale was something that we never tried to take and place under our control. So to the far right. Yes, yes, to the far right. The part of the town controlled by the SDA police and army was taken over by the 1st Corps of the BH Army and later by the 12th Division. They had between 35.000 and 80.000 troops. There were also legitimate targets. Kindergarten Pcelica; elementary school Beta Isakovic [phoen]; Pira's [phoen] cafe; Pastrema [phoen]; Ferhadija, which is a foreign language school; military police on Marsala Tita Street. Sipad, also a civilian facilities. Flats in the well-known elite Carrington building was a legitimate target because it was full of army troops, mortars, and other lethal and combat assets. PAM was -- a PAM was on Vrbanja Most, which is a mortar. So during the trial we are going to establish very precisely and tell you an absolute truth about all these targets were located. The United Nations are going to say that never in Sarajevo it was the Serbs who started fighting. We kept saying, Let us wait for a political solution with the sole purpose of saving people's lives. The Muslims boasted that this internal line towards the city proper was at the beginning of war 42 kilometres long. By the end of war, they boasted of this having extended to 60 kilometres. If you take into account that this was urban warfare, to advance 22 kilometres in city warfare is a clear indication who was attacking in Sarajevo and who was defending themselves in Sarajevo. In Bosnia and in Sarajevo, Serbs never wanted to capture more territories. Quite the contrary. They were prepared to return many important territories for the sake of peace. We never did anything in the town that was contrary to our interests, and our interest was to revive the peace process and to acquire and accomplish three signatures that would spell a peaceful solution. There was never intentional shelling. We are going to prove here that all massive killings were the result of a cunning strategy as called by Sefer Halilovic of Izetbegovic's policy. This was war trick -- these were war tricks aimed at bringing in foreign troops and foreign intervention. And you remember what a judge said in 1983: "What the Young Muslims want can only be achieved through terror or by foreign intervention." The SDA failed to manage to achieve that through terror. They tried to maintain terror and to invite foreign intervention. All the mediators will tell you that everything that happened on Bosnia-Herzegovina that was done by the Muslim side was with the purpose of drawing in NATO and Western countries into war on their side. I am convinced that regardless of all the reforms and innovations in the international jurisprudence, the principle in dubio pro reo is still valid. It is sufficient for us that we know that we can prove that they did shell their own people and that they did kill all their own people from snipers, to demand from the OTP to prove that this was done by the Serbs. We don't need to prove that this was done by the Muslims. Once there is evidence that they did that or they did that as well, then we have to identify which killings were not committed by them and to prove that they were committed by Serbs. Our retaliation, and I think that my letter to General Milovanovic is quoted, where I say that foreign observers are not blaming us for retaliation, but they are just objecting to the number of mortar shells that we are using, and my response was they have more troops but that we had better weapons and I really criticised our side for doing that, but it turned out that that was not exactly true. The fact remains that somebody who didn't have enough troops could retaliate with more mortar shells. You will see from a Presidency session held around the 10th of July that we said, we must reduce the shelling, but in order to do that, we have to bring a brigade from Krajina. We have to maintain a strategic balance, otherwise the people would vanish. It is said in the minutes, Yes, we are going to reduce the shelling, but we have to bring a brigade from the Krajina in order to enable these people to defend themselves. This is not a war between armies, this is the war between peoples. Wherever the SDA army trod, there was nothing left alive. Everything was burned to the ground. The war in Sarajevo lasted for about 1200 days, whereas in the Biblical apocalypse the number is 1260. The city was never under blockade when it was not necessary in military terms. You will see when we talk about the Croats from Bosnia confirming that units were able to enter and exit Sarajevo as they pleased, and you can see from the BH Army orders that a certain brigade should be returned from Igman to the city, etc. Concerning transportation, it was I who proposed at the beginning of war for Sarajevo to become an open city and to be under the control of the UN. Izetbegovic did not accept that. He wanted to have influence on the international community, to use emotional blackmail, stirring up emotions, and thereby provoke intervention. We thought that any restrictions imposed should pertain only to military transports. However, the Sarajevo criminals never allowed commercial traffic, because the prices on the black market would fall if that happened, and they were earning their living from this there, and made a lot of money from it. If you look at the city proper, which was under control of the SDA army, did not get a single drop of water, not a single cubic metre of gas, a single kilowatt of electricity that hadn't crossed the Serbian territory first. We never deprived them of anything of that sort intentionally. How can you call this terrorising the city? Whenever we had a little water, we shared it with them? All the wells are in the Serbian territory, and we shared these water sources with them. There is a letter in which I'm writing to our generals, and they were resentful over the fact that we were allowing all the humanitarian aid to pass through that was distributed only to Muslims and not to Serbs later on, we received maybe one-third or one-fourth, where the accused said that the civilians were not our opponents or our enemies. We are not going to wage war by using water and food. Your Excellencies, in this area between Hrasnica and this narrow passage on the front line is an airfield that we handed over to the United Nations in July 1992. Over 10.000 humanitarian flights landed at this airfield without a single incident from the Serbian side. They shot at the planes occasionally in order to blame us. Ten thousand humanitarian flights, is that terrorising a city? That is what the Serbian side ensured, and it is we who held the airport, and we handed it over to the United Nations. Thousands of convoys of humanitarian aid entered Sarajevo through Serb territory. Trucks and the like. The documentation of General Wahlgren, Mr. Akashi and others will show you that the incident with convoys were only due to irregularities caused by the convoys themselves. That is what Wahlgren explains in his letter and that is confirmed by the representatives of the UN. They say, Serbs do not make any problems regarding convoys, but if there is an extra truck or goods that have not been declared in the bill of entry, then they make a problem. This has to do with simple military reasoning. The soldier has a list of approved goods, and if something is not in line with the list provided, then he says it can’t go through. Another way to create an incident involving a humanitarian convoy for CNN and the like, and there would always be TV crews there: a convoy would show up unannounced at a crossing. There would be a soldier who was not informed, and soldiers did not have the authority to be creative and flexible, as it were. The convoy would be announced at one bridge and then they would appear at another bridge, and the guard there would not know a thing about it. So this is our town. 200.000 Serbs live there. Almost 30.000 declared themselves as Yugoslavs, but almost all of them were Serbs. It's a Serb city as well. I lived that city of my own free will because I loved the city. I love it to this day, and we're never going to give up on it. We have our own part of town. Had our proposal been accepted, that it be declared an open city, there would have been no casualties. Had the transformation of municipalities been agreed to, Serbs, Croats and Muslims, see the brown colour here, all the way up to Ilidza, there would be peace and prosperity. However, a policy that wanted to have 100 per cent authority in 100 per cent of Bosnia against the Christian majority led to what it led to. And the Prosecution believes that we did not have any right whatsoever to protect ourselves or that we had no right to defend ourselves. I would now like to draw your attention to something that I'm going to read out, an excerpt from General Rose's book. He says the reports of the French were a lot more serious.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note, we do not have the text.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "...that the Muslim troops in the city were firing at their own citizens. This was a rule rather than an exception. Bosnian brigadier Hajrulahovic, nicknamed Italian, and General Jovan Divjak were the persons I told that the first examination of the crater of the bomb that had exploded in Markale -- rather grenade, showed that it was fired from the Bosnian side. The room fell silent and Hajrulahovic looked at me in a hostile way. I added that the angle of the shell trajectory proved that it had been fired from a very short distance or perhaps it was planted on the spot and activated. Then I asked him why they moved parts of this."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Given that the interpreters do not have that script, could you slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. Then I asked him why they had removed some parts of the exploded shell before the UN forces had arrived on the spot. You will see, Excellencies, that this Prosecution calls as their witnesses and expert witnesses from the UN people who are not those who are the first to arrive on the scene. We don't see their findings. They call a man who came 40 minutes after the incident, in August 1995, and seven days after the incident in 1994. When we ask these people what the best time is for investigating this kind of incident, they say the very next minute. Right after the incident. That is to say that the first to arrive on the scene stand the best chance of providing accurate findings. The OTP has mislaid or put away those documents or persons who were the first to arrive on the scene, because obviously they don't like their findings. Lord David Owen in his book "The Balkan Odyssey" says, and I quote --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note again we don't have the original document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Muslim government prevented the departure of their own people through internal obstacles and bureaucratic red tape. It was the army, not the government, saying that able-bodied men were not allowed to leave, between the ages and 18 and 45, that is, as well as women -- or, rather, up until the age of 65 and women up until the age of 60 because they were in indispensable for the defence of the city. However, their main reason was different. The Serb siege in the propaganda war led to the compassion of the world. Therefore, it was necessary for the elderly and children to remain there. That was their most emotional propaganda weapon in order to draw the Americans into the war, because they didn't want to get weaker in any way. Furthermore -- so that was the objective, to draw the Americans and NATO into the war. That is what had to do with the shelling of Sarajevo. At one point General Rose says it would be a lot easier if they did not fire at their own people, at their own population. The war would end a lot quicker. We're not talking about in dubio pro reo. We have proof that they did that kind of thing. You saw the footage yesterday of the empty marketplace. You also saw footage of preparations that led to that incident. I am truly surprised not only at the life sentence imposed on General Galic but also by the fact that the OTP continued to use that in the indictments against General Milosevic, myself, et cetera. Therefore, we have to be aware of the fact that it would be a very good thing if the Trial Chamber would instruct the OTP to have a good look at the indictment yet again and to see what -- what the detriment is when there are proceedings only against one side, the weaker one at that, one that was on the defensive all the time, that awaited a political solution. How can that side be declared the belligerent side, the aggressive side, and a terrorist against their own city from which 80 per cent of the Serbian population had been expelled into the suburbs. I believe that if they were to have a careful look at all the material they have available, they would not only withdraw the indictment against me, but they would even ask for a review of the judgements against my generals Galic and Milosevic, in order to save the idea of international justice, to save the idea of courts of this nature. The idea of international justice stands a grave chance of being compromised altogether. If these proceedings continue, I shall prove what it was that happened in Bosnia-Herzegovina. You will see that it is primarily part of the international community that is responsible. First and foremost the SDA, but they could not have done a thing had they not had the encouragement to opt for all or nothing, nothing for the Serbs and the Croats, later on it was nothing for the Croats too, and all for the Islamic fundamentalists, allegedly the Muslim people, but the Muslim people would not have gained anything from this, because the fundamentalists' idea of the structure of power is still Ottoman rather than democratic. You would still have agas and beys, Silajdzic and others, who would be the sole benefactors of such a regime as they would have established. I mean, they would impose that kind of regime and they would be the ones who would get all the benefits. Do we have more time before the break or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We can go on for five minutes, but if you wish, we can take a break now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I thought that perhaps I had said enough about general matters concerning Sarajevo, because during the proceedings we shall be dealing with Sarajevo in detail. This Defence does not agree with the approach taken by the OTP that some Serbs killed some Muslims. We want to know exactly what happened. I still don't have regular forensic material for Markale 1, for Markale 2, for the bread line in Vasa Miskin. For other incidents of mass suffering. I am convinced that in Markale 1 and Markale 2 perhaps there weren't any civilian casualties at all. Perhaps it is corpses that were planted throughout. And the representatives of the UN are going to confirm here that their predecessors had warned them to be very careful about this kind of planting of bodies throughout Sarajevo with a view to accusing the Serb side for that. How are we going to deal with this since we cannot count on objective investigations of an investigating judge, we cannot count on the modesty of the OTP, that they should take care as to what they're doing. We can count on you only and you alone. The Trial Chamber is going to prevent this kind of trickery or planting, and not allow the codification of lies and tricks that are supposed to remain in the history of our people as some kind of truth. We saw yesterday what happened in Markale. It is only someone who wishes to believe that that can believe that, and even that with great difficulty. If you think straight, you see that the Serbs did not do it. You see that it was staged. But do you realise what that does to the people down there, to the Serbs and the Muslims? We're going to talk about Srebrenica today as well. We are going to see what these false myths and false victims do to the souls of the ordinary people who cannot penetrate the essence of the matter. We have to see what this is going to do to the future and what kind of seed of future hatred and suffering has been sown in this way for our children and grandchildren. Whoever believes this, who codifies these things, saying that the Serbs did something that they never did, whoever does that ensured the continuation of further conflicts and slaughters. Whenever there is a crisis in the world, as has been the case so far, it always turns out into a -- turns out be a fratricidal war as well. Perhaps I could stop at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll break for half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Thank you, Excellency. [Interpretation] I'd like now to recapitulate -- or, rather, summarise the facts and enumerate them with respect to the first joint criminal enterprise. I'd like to draw your attention, to have you focus on some facts that we shall be dealing with and easily prove during this trial. I will deal with everything I said in my opening statement, and I dealt with matters that I would easily be able to prove during the trial. The forcible removal of Bosnian Muslims and Croats was never our plan, to begin with. Not ever. It was never in our minds, let alone plans, let alone putting that into practice, and I have been saying over the past two days what proposals the Serbs made, what agreements the Serbs agreed to which absolutely excluded any joint criminal enterprise or common criminal purpose, especially the expulsion of Muslims and Croats from Republika Srpska. We said that we always wanted to live together with the Muslims. We entreated them to remain in Yugoslavia, but that we couldn't agree to come under a Muslim fundamentalist regime in Bosnia, and there's no doubt about the fact that it was such a regime because Mr. Izetbegovic's Islamic Declaration was to be at the core of their constitution. All the agreements, let me remind you, from the five peace plans put forward, this accused agreed to four of them. We reduced to the maximum our wishes and desires and goals in order to avoid war. We bore them down to the very minimum. And I want to remind you of another fact set in stone or marble, this marble fact as I refer to it. There was never a time when some conference on Bosnia and Herzegovina was not in force, at least as of February 1992. Now, let's see what the Serb side was doing and what the Muslim side was doing. The Serb side is bona fides negotiating, and whereas it is taking counter measures of a protective type, should the negotiations fall through, should they be tricked, should we be tricked and deceived. Now, the Prosecution considers that we did not have the right to be cautious when trickery was afoot and then says Karadzic, yes, he did negotiate, but he had a back-up plan. Well, what kind of politician would I be had I not had a back-up plan, had I not had a reserve plan when I knew who I was dealing with. But I didn't -- this back-up plan was not my priority. My priority was negotiation and agreement through negotiation. The SDA did quite the reverse. They falsely negotiated, and they left traces that they engaged in false negotiation, whereas bona fides they were preparing for a war. So the reverse position, and it was God who saved us, not to have gone under in a situation of that kind, where we were negotiating in good faith and were preparing countermeasures in case something went wrong. Now I'm going to put to you an example of what happened in the municipalities. In all the municipalities, agreements were underway about the transformation of those municipalities into two or three municipalities, depending on whether there was a Croat population or two Muslim sets of people or whatever. When the Prosecution says that, "as soon as they took over the municipality," now, where would we -- who would we take the municipality from? From ourselves, of course, for who would we take the Serbian municipalities from, if not from ourselves? We were in power over there. We couldn’t take over the municipality. And I think in paragraph 105, it is, that I've remembered the number correctly, where the Prosecution states that they dismissed people, dismissed Muslims from the police or whatever. Now let's see what really happened. There were Serb municipalities such as Sanski Most, Kljuc, Prijedor, and so on and so forth, but as for Bijeljina, it doesn't say "Serb municipality." For Banja Luka it doesn't say Serb municipality, Pale either. Why? Because there are no conditions for it to become a Muslim municipality. So where it says Serb municipality, the agreement was that it would be a Muslim municipality too. If a Serb municipality had a Serb police force, then negotiations were underway for the Muslims to go to join up with the Muslim police station. So that was the source of what it says here, that the Serbs dismissed people. Why weren't the Muslims dismissed from the Bijeljina police force, Gradiska, Banja Luka? Why were they not dismissed anywhere elsewhere you didn't have a Serb municipality? Not only policemen but every institution which needed -- which wasn't at the level of the town but every Muslim municipality, negotiations were underway. And if it says Serb municipality, then that means that the services were divided there into two municipalities. If it didn't say Serb municipality, let them show me where it is we dismissed someone from, say, Banja Luka or Bijeljina, and we will have a witness coming in, a Muslim from Bijeljina who worked in the police force for as long as he wanted to. Everybody knew he was a Muslim. Nobody killed him. Yes, Muslims and Serbs were killed in Bijeljina but the difference between that is who held the gun. That's the exclusive difference. So you were able to see from Rabija Subic's letter to Izetbegovic, where he is calling upon the fact that he should implement agreements achieved by the Serbs and Muslims in Vlasenica and Bratunac all over Bosnia, that they would have two municipalities side by side and that they would live in peace without interfering with each other. Now, this process of negotiation which served to preserve peace and excluded any kind of population resettlement and transference was brutally interrupted by the SDA party using all resources including the directive for combat readiness straight away, as of the 12th of April. And then pursuant to instructions and orders of the SDA of the 12th of April, all the military-able population was on the move because there was general mobilisation, which meant men from 16 to 65 were called up. It was proclaimed on the 4th of April, and all the soldiers, according to their assertions and documents, over 75 per cent were not in uniform. They did not have a uniform. And for the entire first year of the war, there were no uniforms, and if the person was killed wearing civilian clothing did not mean that it -- he was a civilian. The Serbs didn't have uniforms either but neither about the Muslims. They didn't go to the army. They sabotaged the JNA for a week prior -- for a year prior to that, and they went to war wearing civilian clothes. And if they proved victorious somewhere then they would celebrate and so would their foreign allies. If they were defeated somewhere else, then they would cry out and say that it was an aggression by the aggressor. What aggressor? Whose aggression in Kotor Varos, for instance, or Sanski Most, or Kljujic, inhabited by both the Serbs and Muslims, the local Serbs and the local Muslims? We will have a witness from Prijedor here to confirm -- who will confirm, and he was asked in the Kovacevic case by another counsel, How did you dare? He said, Well, they were better organised than us. They were a better army than us. And counsel asked him, How did you dare to lead your people against an army like that? He said, What could I do? That was the order I received from Sarajevo. So you will see several examples. One is Visegrad and Zvornik. In Visegrad, for instance, which was thrown out of my indictment, removed from my indictment, unfortunately, let me say, there was a terror exercised by the Muslims against the Serbs. There were rapes of young girls on an ethnic basis, and there were killings, and there was the destruction of the monument of Ivo Andric, the Nobel prize winner, a Serb Catholic. They -- some Western countries did not allow Serb Catholics to remain Serbs but Andric always remained a Serb, and in 1991, the monument to Ivo Andric was destroyed. Then there was the saint day killing. Each Serb has a family saint day. They invited two Muslims to attend the luncheon, and at the end, they killed the man for celebrating a Christian saint day in a Muslim Bosnia. They would pull priests by their beards. They would send back people going to Herzegovina on a pilgrimage. They took over -- they stopped the JNA whenever they felt like it. Then the Serbs fled from Visegrad to the surrounding parts and then the army set up law and order again. The Serbs returned, and then the Muslims said that they were attacked for no reason at all. In Zvornik there was also a Muslim reign of terror. The Serbs fled to Karakaj, to the Serbian parts of the municipality. And as for Zvornik, they said that we controlled Zvornik. Well, in Zvornik we controlled the predominantly Serb parts of Zvornik, and when you deduct Sapna, Kovacevic and other areas where Muslims were concentrated, you will see that the rest was not a Muslim majority. Then the Serbs returned, and they recovered, and then they were victorious and then that was considered to be an aggression. Regardless of how much we were actually engaged, that was at the very beginning, so we had no opportunities. In Prijedor a similar situation unfolded itself. The agreement was -- well, first of all they lost on the 12th of April. They were prevented on the 12th of April, and then they got a new order, to attack the whole of the Sana valley Kljuc, Sanski Most, Prijedor, Bosanski Novi, that whole area, as soon as the JNA leaves on 20th of May. So along the Sana River valley they had the elite Patriotic League unit there, and the Sana River valley pursuant to orders from Sarajevo was set aflame. Then we have Sanski Most. I'm still not ready to examine witnesses from Sanski Most, but I do know that there are different types of villages. In certain villages nothing happened. In other villages conflicts and clashes took part. Hrustovo and the others. And they had 900 fighters. And the Muslims write in their books, they say, While we stood guard we didn't have any problems. When we launched an offensive, we were hit on the hands. So we knew that they stood watch, that they had shifts. We didn't mind. That was a defensive measure. If they felt unsafe, let them stand guard, but that's another matter. When they start killing people in Serb villages, then a conflict is unavoidable. So there were two types. There was terror with the Serbs fleeing. Then they came back to protect their homes, their thresholds. Sometimes they were victorious, in other parts not. And then there was this other way of dividing up the municipalities. Sanski Most was Serb. The rest was Muslim. Everything was agreed to, and then they attacked us, and once they lost -- when they lost, we had this hullabaloo created. Twelve thousand Muslims during the war lived in Sanski Most under Serb control. Sanski Most is well known from World War II. There was Susnjar, the hill on which 5.300 Serbs were killed in a single day. So no -- nobody can expect the Serbs to be -- to lack caution and to allow themselves to be killed again that way, on Susnjar. Twelve thousand Muslims live and work in Sanski Most today without any problem and several hundred are at Manjaca, and the difference is only that the ones fought and the others didn't. Now let's take Prijedor, Your Excellencies. The powers in Prijedor, once they had decided to attack, on the 23rd of May, announced this on TV. They shot at car -- at a car with four Serbs and two Croats. Two were killed, two were slightly wounded and two were seriously wounded. You will see how ludicrous it looks when they explain that those six men attacked them at a check-point. That's ludicrous. So when the Muslims started out towards Prijedor, and they did do so, they proclaimed over the radio that the civilians shouldn't leave their homes until they had settled accounts with the terrorists, but many did not listen to that caution, and we'll hear this testimony from many witnesses because they've already made public statements to that effect. Omarska and Keraterm, they weren't camps. Omarska and Keraterm were investigating centres of regular state organs. The Prosecution has and has not disclosed to me over 3.000 documents of the investigations and inquiries undertaken and recorded by the investigating organs in Keraterm and Omarska. 1.500 people were captured in the space of two days. The Croatian intercepts will bear that out as will other sources. There was massive capture of fighters and civilians who had gone out and interfered, but had not fought. So there was this triage in the centre of Omarska and Keraterm and the following results were achieved: 41 per cent had not taken part in any combat and they were released. And then they reached Trnopolje and were safe there because you couldn't have enough policemen to guard every house. But when they were in Trnopolje, then five policemen would be enough to provide security for them, and they confirm this and you will see that on the footage. 41 per cent of the detainees in Keraterm and Omarska were released after this selection and triage on the basis of an investigation. They were Muslims just like the others. They were all Muslims. So 59 per cent were found to be combatants, fighters, and so they were sent to Manjaca, to the military camp there, prisoner of war camp, and 41 per cent were released. Now I'd like the Prosecution to provide me with those 3.000 investigation documents and they should see how these investigations were conducted, because they were normal institutions carried out by the regular organs, not party organs, and then we can see and establish what happened, although it would have been better for this to have been established beforehand. Then we'll see how in a short space of time of the 1.500 that were held in detention, 41 per cent were released. This speaks something which was contrary to what is claimed by the Prosecution, meaning that people who were completely innocent were being arrested and detained. Concerning other relocations or deportations, we are going to prove here, on the basis of documents provided to us by courtesy of the Prosecution, that civilians from both communities asked to be allowed to leave. The Serbs had to pay exorbitant amounts of money to be let out of Sarajevo and Central Bosnia. In Central Bosnia where we were helped in the process by the Croats in some places, because all these Serbs were fleeing, and on the other hand, we also helped Croats and Muslims whenever their civilians needed to be saved and allowed passage. In the areas of Srebrenica and Zvornik, General Morillon was under the constant pressure from both the Serbian and Muslim sides. The Muslims wanted him to take civilians to Tuzla. The Serbs said, All right, we shall allow that, but give us the Serbs from Tuzla. They are suffering there, and they are in danger there. There is no doubt that Morillon was exposed to such pressure. He testified to that, and he enabled the Muslim civilians to leave for Tuzla. Unfortunately, the Muslims of Tuzla did not allow the Serbs to leave Tuzla, and that was the way in which the SDA compromised the SDS in the eyes of the Serbian people, by saying, They're incapable of taking you out of Tuzla. In Nikola Koljevic’s diary, we have evidence that the Muslims from Trebinje via Biljana Plavsic exerted pressure to be allowed to leave Trebinje, which enraged me. According to the diary, I was furious, and I said that it was out of the question. I said if they have any problems, the police is there to protect them. They nevertheless left, as ordered by the SDA, and we have that document which we will present here. And after three months, the SDA wanted to have Trebinje on the basis of ethnic cleansing. These 20 are primitive tricks. We know that they ordered the Trebinje Muslims to go to Montenegro, even though none of them were killed and they didn't come into any harm's way. In Professor Koljevic's diary, who was witness to the events and a participant in them, he was the vice-president of the republic, he was a very responsible person, he was born in Banja Luka, lived in Sarajevo, and had excellent relations with the Muslims, says that one of the international organisations that our side favoured and respected most, i.e. UNHCR and ICRC, demanded that I let a large number of Muslims and Croats from the Bosnian Krajina, the surrounding areas of Banja Luka, to be taken to third countries. That also enraged me and I didn't allow that. After lengthy pressures, I approved five trucks a day to be allowed leave instead of 80, as they requested. If somebody was so much under threat and wanted to be reunited with their families, they were allowed to go. The Prosecutor -- a Prosecution witness in his statement, and he's going to testify here, confirmed this in the very same words. The Prosecution is going to say that it was us who cleansed these people from Bosnia and Krajina. The people from Bosanski Novi actually used UNPROFOR to take them to Croatia. This is what they demanded. Yesterday I said that many municipalities made a lot of obstacles, asking them to provide proof that they had paid taxes and things like that. They created obstacles. That’s not done if you are driving people out of their homes in such fashion that they leave behind them, on the table, a meal that is still warm, as Serbs did when they were fleeing from Muslim areas. The Serbs fled from the Muslim area in a disarray. The Muslims, on the other hand, left the Serbian areas in an orderly fashion, at their own request and escorted by the police, which they had also requested. We are going to prove all this. So the Bosnian Krajina was not cleansed. The Croatian minister, who is now in the Government of Republika Srpska, recently said, "I never left Republika Srpska. Those who left were angry with me for staying behind." So his own fellow Croats who left Doboj left in order to exploit this fact, and they were angry at him for staying behind and thereby negating his -- their claim that it will -- a co-existence with Serbs was impossible. We have an interview with this minister. So we are going to refute these things, and I believe that we are -- believe that that was untrue. We are going to prove that not a single village that surrendered their weapons or didn't have them at all in the first place had no problems. Not a single Muslim who was not engaged in fighting had any problems. Those who were imprisoned were extremists without exception. I would now like to move to the subject of Srebrenica and the elimination of Muslims from Srebrenica by organised killing of men and by deportation of women and children and genocide of the Srebrenica Muslim. Here in this title there are no men and boys mentioned without the Prosecution explaining what "boy" means, but this is an emotional impact which implies that the Serbs were killing boys. When you say a boy, it could be a 16 or 17 boy who was mobilised and who was a member of a unit. Quite briefly let me tell you this – so that it does not appear to be tu quoque – it’s not tu quoque – that there was fierce fighting and there was terrible terror exercised by the Muslims of the area. They shot at the army in the back, and no army in the world shall tolerate that. They killed entire villages on Christian holidays, on Christmas and slavas. And this is clear, it’s available, it is easy to prove. This accused issued orders to exercise maximum restraint during all Catholic and Muslim holidays. And in both this war and the Second World War, they killed Serbs on their biggest holidays. You will see here what they did in Kravica in 1993, this was eight or nine months after the war broke out. On Christmas Day, they slaughtered people who were caught unawares, while preparing for the festivities, without any reason whatsoever, and that was actually an attack on civilians that was provoked by nothing. I'm going to request the Prosecution to provide reliable information about how many Muslim women and children were killed and how many Serb women and children were killed, and we are going to demonstrate where it was that the Serbs were being killed and where the Muslims were being killed, and both these groups were mostly killed in Serbian villages. The Muslim army attacks a Serbian village and the result is end of both Serbs and Muslims. The place of death will clearly demonstrate what -- what was being done by everyone in this war. Before I move to Srebrenica, let me tell you something about directive. We are talking here about directives 4 and 7, these two directives, and I'm not going to go into this whether I signed any of this, but I will focus on what General Mladic said about them leaving the zone together with the population. The population made an ultimatum and wanted to be allowed to leave. In November, in Kotor Varos, there was an uprising among the Muslims, and they wanted their population to be allowed to go, and I approved of that. Mladic, not knowing about that, said no. They cannot just allow the civilians to go and they would remain there and fight against us in our territory. Two weeks after that, Mladic issued directive number 4, relating to Eastern Bosnia, and he says the same thing, that they would either leave alongside with the civilians or disarm themselves and remain to live as civilians. And the Prosecution translates this as "surrender themselves", disarm oneself and surrender oneself. We have a problem with the transcript, don't we. Directive number 4, there is a sentence in this directive which is perpetuated further on in directive 7, and this sentence, which is ascribed to both Mladic and me, says that we had ordered for the civilians to disappear from a certain area, but that is not true. What Mladic said was that the fighters should leave together with the civilians and not the civilians with the fighters. We are going to prove that it was the civilians who asked and who were given permission to leave. Then Mladic added that, You shall also go with them. Mladic didn't say the army should leave and take civilians with them, but quite the opposite. If the civilians are going to leave, then the army should join them. There's no doubt about that. Two weeks before directive 4 was issued we had this case in Kotor Varos and now this case has become a pattern of the Serbian conduct. If the civilians want to leave, you should leave with them and not stay behind and to shoot us in the back. The essence of directive 4 and directive 7 was that the civilians should take the army with them, because the civilians wanted to leave in any case. These requests were made in Eastern Bosnia to Morillon and in Kotor Varos to the municipal War Presidency. It was an ultimatum for their civilians to be allowed to leave. There is proof that I said it's all right, allow them safe passage. But soldiers have their own logic. They would say why -- why would you leave and allow civilians to leave without army joining them? We cannot allow that. Well, that is the basis for Directives 4 and 7, which the OTP is waving around and based on which they have convicted some people, but it is not correct at all. This sentence says that the army should join civilians, not the other way around, and it has been established that two weeks prior to that the civilians were allowed to leave Kotor Varos, and that the army was ordered to leave together with them and not stay behind our backs, deep in our territory, and fight us. As for Srebrenica, I will just briefly describe the period before 1995. In 1993, Srebrenica and Zepa were declared safe zones after I halted the advance of Serbian Army. We had been under constant attack from that area, from Kamenica, from the surrounding places between Srebrenica and Zvornik. They were constantly attacking us, and not only the army. They would set an ambush and they would kill a bus full of civilians, as they did at Crni Vrh. That's what was impossible to tolerate any longer. The negotiations did not yield any results. They followed orders from Sarajevo to provoke the Serbian Army everywhere they could. That is how fighting took place in the area around Zvornik, Kamenica, towards Srebrenica, which they lost. Many of them went to Srebrenica. There was enormous propaganda surrounding Cerska. The same like the one concerning Srebrenica. There was rivers of blood. The Serbs were slaughtering people. General Morillon wanted to enter Cerska to see for himself, which he did, and he reported that there was no fighting whatsoever, let alone massacre. For that reason we were late in ordering an investigation to be carried out regarding Srebrenica, because the same propaganda that was applied to Cerska was repeated two years later to Srebrenica. I halted the advance of our army towards Srebrenica with the well-known order I gave. It has been presented here. And I even ordered them not to investigate any crime -- war crimes, although there were lots of them, just to avoid any revenge killings. A border between the two safe zones were agreed, and the passage was left between Skelani and Milici. Throughout the whole period, as testified by the UN Secretary-General, Srebrenica and Zepa were not safe haven, but they were, rather, military strongholds of armed troops from which at least one Serb was killed daily by shooting from these zones. We have daily reports of the Secretary-General to the Security Council about what was happening there. The Prosecution, probably based on that, accepted that these were legitimate operations, but our operation was not aimed at capturing Srebrenica. In all the agreements, in all peace plans we had accepted that Srebrenica and Zepa would be connected to Gorazde and that it would become a canton, as is the case today with Gorazde, and Zepa and Srebrenica would be Muslim. Therefore, we never even thought of taking them. All of a sudden it turns out, once all soldiers enter Srebrenica, that they had left Srebrenica. That's when I ordered them to enter the town to restore peace and order. I have that letter here too. General Tolimir, in particular, was informed of what I had approved. Once they entered Srebrenica there were no civilians in sight nor any members of the military. The army fled to the woods. The civilian authority surrenders. The army didn't listen to the civilian authorities. They fled to the forests and wanted to continue fighting. And the civilian population were not taken out of their homes by the Serb army but, rather, by the UN. We also have the testimony of Muslim witnesses here that, starting out from the villages, and not from Srebrenica itself, they went with the plan and intention for men to join the units to make a breakthrough towards Tuzla, whereas the civilians were supposed to go to Potocari and then to be taken by UNPROFOR to Kladanj and Muslim-held territory. Our entry was a complete surprise but also any -- also the absence of civilians in the houses was a surprise. The Prosecution still insists, nevertheless, that this was a forcible deportation, whereas we have every possible evidence that that was not the case and that was never planned. When we heard that they wanted to leave their homes and to be transferred to Kladanj and Tuzla under Muslim control, we hastily started looking for buses and trucks to provide for transportation because we were afraid of revenge, of acts of revenge. If someone bent on revenge threw a grenade into such a crowd, there would be a massacre. There had been no killing until the 14th. There was some incident on the 13th, in Kravica, when a Muslim detainee grabbed a rifle and started shooting. That was when an incident occurred. The crown witness of the Prosecution against me in the Srebrenica case was late Deronjic, and they laid all their hopes in him according to 92 quater rule. He actually testified in my favour. He said that on the evening of the 13th and morning of the 14th, there was a colonel who was allegedly wanting to kill certain detainees and that he prevented them from doing that. He told him, "If you keep behaving like that, I'm going to call the president." That was on the 13th in the evening, and he eventually withdrew. We have a language problem here between the terms "detainees" and "prisoners of war." When we speak about prisoners, this is not a detainee in our language. When you say "prisoner," that implies a prisoner of war, and those who are detained are called detainees. So we are talking about POWs. And when we speak about an exchange of prisoners without saying "prisoners of war," then the Prosecution claims that this was an exchange of detainees. This is another linguistic problem that we are facing here. Once you say a prisoner, it is understood that this means a prisoner of war captured in fight. Those who were detained were detained on a different basis and due to different reasons. Thank you for this correction in the transcript. On the morning of the 14th, as testified to by Deronjic, I don't know whether that actually happened or not with that colonel, but Deronjic himself says, "I met him at Yellow Bridge, and he asked that we use the brick factory, and I said I'm going to Pale to see the president." And indeed he did come to see me on the 14th, and then this man withdrew. A member of -- a small town SDS president stops a member of the Main Staff twice by using the name of Radovan Karadzic. Had Radovan Karadzic ordered some kind of unlawful killing, the colonel would have said, "What do you want, kid? I have my instructions." Even if Mladic had said something to him, he would say, "What do I care about you? I have my boss. See?" So the strongest Prosecution witness, according to what has been said so far, absolutely does not speak in favour of the thesis that is advocated by the Prosecution. Deronjic testifies also to the fact that allegedly he said to me on the 14th that some officers want to kill prisoners of war and that I said that all these officers were crazy. The driver who brought him testifies to the following: When Deronjic returned from me, when he got into the car, he said, "I cannot believe that the president knows nothing about this." The OTP knows that. I don't remember about him having said that. If he made an allusion, perhaps I didn't understand it, but saying that officers were crazy, well, there was a quite a bit of tension between the officers and the civilian authorities. We held a lot of things against each other. But when a psychiatrist said that somebody is crazy, then that may sound like a diagnosis, but this wasn't a diagnosis. This was just speaking figuratively. So they cannot use Deronjic against me and they really don't have anything else. Then there's the report of the Dutch government that says that Karadzic's role is unclear. In dubio pro reo is the rule that prevails. Therefore, there is no culpability. There is no investigation. There is no investigation for Srebrenica. I cannot say anything about Srebrenica because there is no investigation. What they created there was a place of worship. It's a myth again. On the stone there it says "Over 8.000 Muslims," and they could not bury more than 2.500. I don't know what the exact figure is now, but please have a look at where these Muslims come from, those who were buried on this hallow ground. See, Bratunac; Bijeljina, that is 100 kilometres away from there; Foca; Han Pijesak; Rogatica, Sarajevo; Sokolac; Srebrenica; Srebrenik, which is even further away; Ugljevik; Visegrad; Vlasenica; and Zvornik. And now what they're saying is that the Serbs killed Muslim boys and men, 8 .320. Over four years of war, deaths during the course of four years of war, deaths in forests around Srebrenica when attempts were made to forcibly break through Serb territory. Nevertheless, including all of that, they could not bury more than 2.000, 3.000 people. And then this investigating material. People are being tried for Srebrenica here and this investigating material is being dealt with just like that. Let us see where the DNA is. Now I am in the stage of establishing the truth concerning Srebrenica. Let us see whether there was anything unlawful, whether there was any unlawful killing, how did it happen, and what the extent of it was, if any. However, we have the report of the Muslim municipality itself that says we have 37.000 people. We are showing 45 for the sake of humanitarian aid so that we could feed our troops too. So if we are to add up natural deaths and death in -- deaths in combat and also all of those who managed to get out of Kladanj and Tuzla, and when we see what they identified and in which day they identified the cause of death, executions do not take place by shells. There have to be investigations for the sake of the future, not for Karadzic's sake, for the sake of the future of the peoples over there. It has to be established who got killed how and in which way and where. But just to have trials off-the-cuff saying such and such a number of Serbs killed such and such a number of Muslims, I hope this Trial Chamber is not going to support that. Let it be established once and for all what happened in Srebrenica. I have to say that I cannot accuse Trial Chambers of not having established that, because in our system it is the investigating judges who are in charge. However, the Defence teams were not in a position to present the truth to the Trial Chambers involved because there was no investigation. Simply there was no investigation, and there was no way of saying this happened or that happened because there was no proper investigation. Now, after the investigation concerning Srebrenica, and I am going to ask for each and every report that exists, I have been given the consent of the Trial Chamber to receive all the material involved, all the information, and then let us create a 5 per cent sample of the DNA and then let us see whether there are significant deviations. If that is the case, then everything has to be examined. You see, we know to this day that graves are being exhumed in Bosnia and Herzegovina, all over Bosnia and Herzegovina so that somebody could be buried in July in Srebrenica. Well, of course the death of a single person is significant, but then why exaggerate. I have another 15 minutes left; is that right? I would like to say, finally, something about paragraph 11 -- or, rather, joint criminal enterprise that pertains to hostage-taking. My essential objection is that an army cannot be held hostage. Civilians are hostages, and they are not taking part in fighting in any way. These gentlemen who were held hostage, if I can put it that way, were not civilians, and they were involved in combat. Let me say straight away it's going to be easy for me to prove that I have nothing to do with that. A Prosecution witness said Karadzic found out from the media and the entire world without out from the media that people were panic-stricken before the unlawful air-strikes by NATO, unlawful bombing, because this was not close-air support, which would have been legitimate if a UN unit had been endangered. However, this operative [indiscernible] was bombing the Serb positions, and it was a strategic decision in order to weaken the position of the Serbs so that they could not defend themselves easily. The Serbs kept these foreigners close to a bridge so that that bridge would not be hit, because in a different situation, the SDA would have slaughtered them -- or, rather, their army would have slaughtered them. The general said in his first interview, Karadzic found out from the media. He called and said that they should be released straight away. However, that could not have been helped any longer. The media had already carried these news and everyone started takes these hostages. Why are they not hostages, though? Why are they combatants? We are going to prove here that all UN generals are asking their civilian chiefs, "Please do not involve us in the conflict. You're going to expose to us to danger, and you are going to make us become part of one of the sides involved." All of the commanders were aware that if they bombed the Serbs, with a call made to these troops, that these troops will be involved. And it's not that they were involved through the action of their commanders only. They were even involved individually. General Rose has the transcript of a broadcast as to how his soldiers were involved, because they were the marksmen of the aircraft flying above them. And then this young man says, "I have chosen a target and I can hear the aircraft. I have the target -- oh, my goodness. The Serbs hit my target. My target falls," and so on and so forth. Let us leave aside what our suspicions are and what our proven suspicions are to the effect that these UN units were involved in smuggling. For a while UNPROFOR was called the taxi of the Muslim army because they crossed our lines unannounced. They smuggled ammunition, weapons, but nobody would have taken them as hostages because of that. They were taken as hostages when the bombing started, not for the sake of close-air support but tactically, operatively and almost strategically for other reasons. Now, all of these military observers, we have a witness who says that -- says that these people are experts, and one such individual is more valid than an entire company of mine. I am very sorry that they bombed us in the first place, but I am sorry that this was done, but this is not hostage-taking. They were involved in a war against us. They called NATO aircraft to bomb us. They helped them. They selected targets for them. They were their marksmen. Well, people like that cannot be called hostages. So you will see during the Defence case how many foreign soldiers in Bosnia were killed by the Muslim side. You will see that they downed the Italian aircraft. The Serbian Army couldn't have done that in any way. And then a no-fly zone was introduced after that. You'll see how many times the Muslims shelled convoys that were escorted by UNPROFOR from Igman. All of this we have on the basis of the material that the OTP has and uses against me. You will see what they did to the foreigners who smuggled weapons for them, gave them vast amounts of humanitarian aid. They shelled them. They hit them with sniper fire in order to cause odium against the Serbs. Actually it was clear and it was unequivocally established that they were the ones who were doing that. You will not find a single case except for one that the Serbs did that. A lieutenant-colonel, when he became very nervous, he did not kill anyone but he simply scattered the things belonging to a convoy all over the place. I apologised to Mr. Wahlgren, and I dismissed this man. His nerves were shaken and he was upset because UNPROFOR was interfering and doing all sorts of things that they were not supposed to do. But the most important thing is what the UNPROFOR commander says, Do not get us involved against the war. We will become a warring party if you involve us in this. And the moment when they started bombing us outside the close-air support, they did become a warring party. Now, I don't need to dwell on this any longer. Suffice it to say that soldiers who take a particular side, regardless of what their weapon is, a laser or a rifle or whatever else, they cannot be hostages. They are combatants. They are fighting against one of the sides that can at least take them prisoner. Of course that was not a decision taken by civilian authorities, it was not a decision taken by the military commands, but it did so happen that the people did that, and we have proof of that in OTP material. I remember that that was the case. I remember that the images were carried all over the world, and it was hard to release them silently because the bombing was going on and the people all of a sudden realised that that would save us. Excellencies, I'm not afraid of these proceedings. It is with great enthusiasm that I am preparing for these proceedings. Regrettably this may endanger my health because I'm working all night because I don't have enough time. Why do I not have enough time? Because inter alia for three and a half or four months, whatever, I did not have proper assistance. My advisors could not work with me, and the OTP had indiscriminately thrown together loads of material and alleged evidence guided by the fact that they did not have evidence. And then, like our Marxists, they thought that some day quantity would become quality, or that it's better to use a shotgun against a little bird and then you will hit one at least. If the Security Council does not pass a Resolution sanctioning the agreement with Holbrooke on my immunity, I am going to tell you what I'm thinking about. I don't know whether all of it is possible, but I'll tell you what I think. I think it would be a good thing if the Trial Chamber were to return the indictment to the OTP, to see all the things that they presented there that can easily be swept up as false evidence. So they should either amend the indictment, narrow down the indictment, and they cannot just say that Karadzic's intentions can be heard through Tom, Dick, and Harry's words. I'm a politician. I make speeches. If I have an intention to carry out something, I have to pacify people, and it is deeds that speak, not words. If they don't want to withdraw the indictment, if they don't want to reduce the indictment, if they don't want to isolate the things that really pertain to me, then it would be a good thing for me to get time and resources, because the President of the Tribunal also established that I did not have sufficient resources, so let us have exemplary proceedings that will be to the credit of the Trial Chamber, the OTP, and Defence. Exemplary proceedings that is going to be a blueprint for international justice, that is going to rehabilitate international courts and trials of this nature. In that case, I could take it upon myself, up until the end of May or, say, mid-June, if the trial were to be resumed in mid-June, then by the second half of May I could provide you with thousands of facts, my agreed facts list. These are facts that the OTP will not be able to challenge, practically not at all. For example, that Serbs took over such and such a municipality, and Serbs lived there in the first place. For example, Hadzici was under Serb control. Serbs held under their control only a very part -- a small part of Hadzici. Only the Serbian neighbourhood there, actually. So these are facts that we could agree on. By the end of May or, say, by mid-May I could provide these agreed facts and this would disburden these proceedings. We could agree on so many things. That would shorten the proceedings to a maximum of, say, one or one and a half year, because there would be very few facts that would be challenged and that we would be dealing with here in this courtroom. Your Excellencies, I would like to end on that note, and I think that the best thing would be to observe the Holbrooke Agreement, because that actually did take place. However, somebody did not do their work. I did my share. Could the Office of the Prosecutor ask you to have the indictment withdrawn? However, if we are going to go to trial, then there are going to be reviews of other trials where innocent men were convicted. I will be able to prove that they were convicted as innocent men as I defend myself here in these proceedings. If we go to trial, then I'm going to do whatever is up to me. If we are going to have expeditious, fair proceedings that will be to the credit of the international community and international justice, I am going to give a constructive contribution, as I have been doing all along. And my constructive contribution is going to be in singling out the facts that we can all agree upon, and in this way, we can cleanse these proceedings from unnecessary material that would just exhaust us here. We have to go to the basic merits of this case. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. This is an oral ruling of the Chamber. Following the Trial Chamber's decision on the accused's motion for the postponement of trial, issued on 26 February 2010, the accused yesterday filed an application for certification to appeal and for stay. The Prosecution responded to that application yesterday, stating that it does not oppose the granting of certification to appeal the Trial Chamber's decision but that it does oppose staying the proceedings until such time as the Appeals Chamber determines the matter. Pursuant to Rule 73(B) of the Tribunal's Rules, a Trial Chamber may grant certification to appeal one of its decisions if that decision "involves an issue that would significantly affect the fair and expeditious conduct of the proceedings or the outcome of the trial, and for which, in the opinion of the Trial Chamber, an immediate resolution by the Appeals Chamber may materially advance the proceedings." Having considered the submission of the parties, the Chamber is satisfied that the issue of the accused's readiness to actively participate in his trial at this stage of the proceedings, which is determined in the Chamber's decision on postponement, pertains directly to the fairness of the proceedings and that therefore the first prong of the test for certification under Rule 73(B) is met in the present circumstances. Since a resolution of this matter at any later stage could require in the specific circumstances of this case a retrial in the event that the Trial Chamber decision is found to have been incorrect, the Trial Chamber is satisfied that the second prong of the test is also met. Given that both prongs of the test for certification are satisfied and the Chamber's view that it is in the interests of justice for the Appeals Chamber to rule on this issue, certification to appeal is hereby granted. The Trial Chamber is mindful of the fact that staying the proceedings at this stage would have an adverse effect on witnesses who have already been brought to The Hague to testify this week and next. However, should the proceedings continue tomorrow with the hearing of those witnesses' evidence and the Appeals Chamber subsequently overturn the Trial Chamber's decision on postponement, those witnesses would have to return to The Hague for a third time and repeat their testimony as would all the other witnesses whose evidence was heard between now and the Appeals Chamber's decision. Having considered the matter carefully, the Trial Chamber is thus convinced that it is in the interests of justice for it to stay the effect of its decision on postponement until the Appeals Chamber resolves the matter. The Chamber regrets the inconveniences caused to those witnesses who have already travelled to The Hague or who are in transit, and trusts that the Appeals Chamber will resolve this matter speedily so that we can proceed to hear their evidence as soon as possible. Plainly, it is in everyone's interest that both sides use any time available before the Appeals Chamber's decision to continue with active trial preparation. Therefore, now that Mr. Karadzic's opening statement has concluded, these proceedings will be adjourned until further order following the Appeals Chamber's ruling. The hearing is now adjourned.
